One realises how special a talent the Masters champion is when reaching 15 under par despite missing chance upon chance. McIlroy’s 68 included four birdie misses from 10ft or closer. His irritation at what might have been can be partly offset by the making up of decent ground on Patrick Reed in the DP World Tour’s order of merit race. Reed versus McIlroy promises to be quite the spectacle between now and mid November.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toSport in FocusOur picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown inEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“I feel like my game is heading in the right direction,” said McIlroy, who is in the midst of technical changes. “When I look at my swing on video, I still don’t like what I am seeing. It is going to take time.Golfisn’t just about the swing, you also have to chip and putt. My swing is not where I want it to be.” Still, McIlroy produced the shot of the day with an iron from trees at the 12th which hooked 80 yards before resting just short of the green.Joost Luiten, Matt Fitzpatrick, Ryan Fox and Filippo Celli completed the top nine. This was, however, a story dominated by one man. And not, given the circumstances, the one who came out on top.Explore more on these topicsEuropean TourRory McIlroyGolfnewsShareReuse this content

title: NFL roundup: Bears QB Caleb Williams carted off in loss to Vikings; Saints stun Ravens  | NFL | The Guardian
description: Chicago lost quarterback Caleb Williams to a hamstring injury in their loss to Minnesota, while there was a shock result in Baltimore
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Chicago lost quarterback Caleb Williams to a hamstring injury in their loss to Minnesota, while there was a shock result in Baltimore
Content: Caleb Williams was hurt on a non-contact play.Photograph: Patrick McDermott/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenCaleb Williams was hurt on a non-contact play.Photograph: Patrick McDermott/Getty ImagesNFLNFL roundup: Bears QB Caleb Williams carted off in loss to Vikings; Saints stun RavensCaleb Williams leaves game with leg injuryTyler Shough’s late touchdown cheers New OrleansAgenciesSun 20 Sep 2026 16.34 EDTLast modified on Sun 20 Sep 2026 19.41 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMinnesota Vikings 9–3 Chicago BearsCarson Wentz passed for 143 yards, Aaron Jones Sr. rushed for 105 yards, and the visiting Minnesota Vikings (2-0) escaped ⁠with a 9-3 win over theChicago Bears, who lost their quarterback to a hamstring injury.In the fourth quarter, Williams’s injury cast a pall over the Soldier Field crowd on a gloomy, wet day along the lakefront. The Bears (1-1) trailed by three points but had first-and-goal from the Vikings’ six-yard line with less than eight minutes to go. Williams kept the ball ‌and sprinted to his left with ample green space in front of him.Suddenly, Williams stumbled and fell to his knees on a ​non-contact play. He rolled over a few times in pain until the Bears’ medical staff attended to him. He appeared to fight emotions as he was carted from the sideline ⁠to the locker room. The Bears said Williams suffered a hamstring injury.“I mean you could kind of see in real time. I’m actually happy it’s nothing with the knee,” Bears coach Ben Johnson said. “That was my first inclination. But yeah, a hamstring can be pretty damaging as well. We’ll see how bad it is tomorrow and we’ll go from there. It’s quickly you’ve got to turn the page.”Wentz completed 11 of 20 passes in ⁠his 100th career start ⁠as Minnesota (2-0) won ​despite failing to score a touchdown. Justin Jefferson had three catches for 55 yards.New Orleans Saints 24–17 Baltimore RavensTyler Shough scored on a fourth-down sneak with 1:28 remaining, and the New Orleans Saints (1-1) rallied to victory over the Baltimore Ravens (1-1). New Orleans had first down from the two before a penalty and a costly incomplete pass. On fourth-and-goal, the Saints decided against a short field goal, and Shough was ruled to have scored on a sneak. The play was upheld after a review. The Ravens, who didn’t have a first down on either of their previous two drives, made it to the New Orleans 37, but Lamar Jackson’s deep pass was intercepted by Julian Blackmon with 13 seconds left.Jacksonville Jaguars 13–20 Denver BroncosThe Denver Broncos snapped the Jacksonville Jaguars’ nine-game regular-season winning streak. Jaylen Waddle and Jonah Coleman led a big second-half comeback for the Broncos. Waddle had eight catches for 138 yards, and Coleman scored a three-yard touchdown run midway through the fourth quarter. The Broncos trailed 13-3 but responded with a field goal and a touchdown pass from Bo Nix to Nate Adkins before Coleman’s tiebreaking TD. The Jaguars had built a 13-3 lead with a touchdown run and two field goals. The Broncos tightened their defense and secured the win. Both teams are 1-1 after two games.Cincinnati Bengals 20–6 Houston TexansJoe Burrow threw two touchdown passes to Ja’Marr Chase and the Cincinnati Bengals are off to their second straight 2-0 start after notching ⁠a road victory over the Houston Texans. Burrow completed 20 of 31 passes for 207 yards and Chase had seven receptions for ⁠75 yards while posting ⁠his 14th career ​outing of two or more touchdown catches. Chase had just two catches for 12 yards in Week 1. CJ Stroud was 30-of-55 passing ⁠for 353 yards for the Texans (0-2), who lost at home for the second straight week. Dalton Schultz ​established career bests of 12 catches for 140 yards ‌for Houston, who lost ‌despite registering five sacks.Miami Dolphins 13–35 San Francisco 49ersChristian McCaffrey became the fourth-fastest player in the Super Bowl era with 100 career touchdowns, Brock Purdy played a near-perfect game and the San Francisco 49ers (2-0) overwhelmed the Miami Dolphins (0-2). The 49ers showed no signs of fatigue after beating the Los Angeles Rams in their opener in Australia and have started the season with back-to-back wins of at least 20 points for the first time in franchise history. They scored touchdowns on their first five drives of the game. Miami were dominated after spending the week by practicing in nearby Napa after losing their opener in Las Vegas.Las Vegas Raiders 26–14 Los Angeles ChargersKirk Cousins passed for 253 yards and three touchdowns while the defense forced a key turnover with less than four minutes ⁠remaining as the Las Vegas Raiders earned a victory over the Los Angeles Chargers. Tre Tucker caught five passes ⁠for 119 yards and ⁠a long ​first-half touchdown, while Cody White had two catches, both for touchdowns, as the Raiders (2-0) ended a five-game road losing streak against the Chargers and ⁠a seven-game road losing streak overall. Cousins was 19-of-29 passing with an interception while becoming the first Raiders quarterback with at least three TD passes in the ⁠first two games of a season since Ken Stabler in 1976. Justin Herbert was 15-of-27 passing for 192 ​yards with a touchdown and two interceptions ‌as the Chargers (0-2) saw a ‌four-game overall winning streak against the Raiders come to an end.Seattle Seahawks 31–7 Arizona CardinalsDrew Lock threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns to Jaxon Smith-Njigba in a stellar first start subbing for the injured Sam Darnold and the Seattle Seahawks (2-0) continued their dominance over the Arizona Cardinals (1-1). The defending Super Bowl champions have now won 10 straight over their NFC West rival dating to 2022 and closed this one by scoring the final 24 points. Smith-Njigba finished with nine catches for 155 yards and the career-high three TDs in one of the best performances of his career.Washington Commanders 20–37 Dallas CowboysDak Prescott broke Tony Romo’s franchise record for touchdown passes with four in the Dallas Cowboys’ (1-1) victory over the Washington Commanders (0-2). Prescott’s record-breaking TD toss was a 24-yarder to receiver CeeDee Lamb in the fourth quarter, the 249th of his career. It was their second TD connection of the game after Prescott had already thrown a pair to tight end Jake Ferguson. The 33-year-old Prescott has thrown 37 TDs to Lamb, the most of any target. The only major category left for Prescott to take over first place in the history of the storied franchise will be victories.Pittsburgh Steelers 3–20 New England PatriotsTreVeyon Henderson ran for a 39-yard touchdown in his season debut, Eli Ponder added a 19-yard fumble recovery for a score and the New England Patriots’ defense smothered Aaron Rodgers on the way to victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers (1-1). With the victory, Patriots coach Mike Vrabel avoided just the second 0-2 start of his eight-year coaching career. Romeo Doubs had a 63-yard catch in the third quarter to set up Andy Borregales’ second field goal of the game. Drake Maye finished 14 of 22 for 208 yards and an interception. Rodgers struggled to deal with the Patriots’ defensive pressure. The 42-year-old fumbled twice, including the one that led to Ponder’s score.Green Bay Packers 20–17 New York Jets (OT)The Green Bay Packers (1-1) overcame a 10-point fourth-quarter deficit to snap a six-game losing streak with an overtime win against the New York Jets (1-1). Trey Smack kicked a 26-yard field goal to secure the victory. Jordan Love threw two touchdown passes for the Packers, despite the team committing 14 penalties. The Jets, who also struggled with penalties, couldn’t hold their lead. Geno Smith was sacked twice in overtime, forcing the Jets to punt. Love then led a drive that set up Smack’s game-winning kick.Philadelphia Eagles 24–20 Tennessee TitansJalen Hurts threw a three-yard touchdown pass to Darius Cooper with nine seconds left, and the Philadelphia Eagles (2-0) beat the Tennessee Titans (0-2). The Eagles appeared ready to dominate Tennessee on a hot and steamy Sunday. They opened the game by stringing together three straight drives of at least 11 plays. The Titans sacked Hurts three times and picked him off twice, turning those into 10 points. The second interception set up Joey Slye’s 33-yard field goal with 1:56 left, putting Tennessee up 20-17 before Hurts, who finished with 264 yards passing and two TDs, helped his team to victory.Cleveland Browns 23–19 Tampa Bay BuccaneersDeshaun Watson earned at least a few more starts for the Cleveland Browns (1-1). Watson threw two touchdown passes, including a go-ahead 17-yard toss to Blake Whiteheart in the fourth quarter, leading the Browns to a comeback victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-2) in a game that was delayed two hours, 12 minutes because of lightning. The Buccaneers were driving and had a second-and-4 at the Cleveland 28 when the game was suspended at the two-minute warning. When the game finally resumed, heavy rain started falling again, and the Bucs could not pull off the win.Carolina Panthers 34–3 Atlanta FalconsBryce Young threw for 287 yards and three touchdowns, including two to Darren Waller, Carolina’s Devin Lloyd returned one of his two interceptions for a touchdown and the Panthers (1-1) crushed the short-handed Atlanta Falcons (0-2). The Panthers took their fourth straight win in the NFC South rivalry. Young completed 23 of 36 passes as he improved to 5-1 against the Falcons. He set a franchise record with 448 yards passing in a 30-27 overtime win to cap last season’s sweep. With Cooper Rush at quarterback, the Falcons had more offensive woes. Rookie Jack Strand replaced Rush late in the game.Explore more on these topicsNFLUS sportsChicago BearsnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘We miss her the same every day’: Olivia Cusack on her late footballer sister Maddy | Women's football | The Guardian
description: Olivia Cusack tells Tom Garry of her determination to ensure Maddy’s ‘legacy lives on’ three years after the Sheffield United player’s death
Author: Tom Garry
Headline: Olivia Cusack tells Tom Garry of her determination to ensure Maddy’s ‘legacy lives on’ three years after the Sheffield United player’s death
Content: Olivia Cusack (left, with Maddy) and her loved ones are enduring a ‘frustrating and confusing’ wait for answers about the circumstances surrounding her death.Photograph: Olivia CuscakView image in fullscreenOlivia Cusack (left, with Maddy) and her loved ones are enduring a ‘frustrating and confusing’ wait for answers about the circumstances surrounding her death.Photograph: Olivia CuscakWomen's footballInterview‘We miss her the same every day’: Olivia Cusack on her late footballer sister MaddyExclusive interview byTom GarryFamily is determined to ensure her ‘legacy lives on’ three years after the Sheffield United player’s deathSun 20 Sep 2026 03.00 EDTLast modified on Sun 20 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleOlivia Cusack says her sister, the late Maddy Cusack, is on her mind every single day and she is determined to ensure her “legacy lives on” three years after the former England youth international midfielder’s death.Olivia, together with family and friends of Maddy, walked 29 miles from Bramall Lane, Sheffield United’s home, to their family’s home in Horsley, near Derby, on Saturday to raise funds and awareness. Maddy’s loved ones are still enduring a “frustrating and confusing” wait for answers about the circumstances surrounding her death on 20 September 2023.An inquest into the death of the 27-year-old Sheffield United playerwas adjourned again in Julyand has been scheduled to resume on 7 December after fresh evidence came to light. Cusack, a former England under-19 international, was the first player to appear in 100 matches for the Sheffield United women’s team.Olivia says the walk on Saturday, “Bringing Maddy Home”, was motivated by some of the evidence during the inquest. “After the inquest we wanted to bring her home from Bramall Lane, back to our family home,” she says. “Many people know Maddy as the professional football player and the name on the back of her shirt, the number, the colours she wore, the club she was associated with.“But I felt in the inquest it was lost that she was a person, she wasn’t an object that we were discussing. She’s a person, she’s a family member of ours [and] a person that’s sometimes been lost within the chaos surrounding her death really, so that’s the notion behind the walk. To claim her back, bring her home and protect her.”A minute’s applause will be held before kick-off on Sunday at the Women’s Super League 2 fixture between Newcastle and Sheffield United. Discussing that anniversary, Olivia says: “We miss her the same every day, as I will on Sunday. The anniversary is always something that creeps up on us. It’s very emotional and it’s a time where we just reflect, but we do so much throughout the year so she really is at the heart of pretty much every single day. Not a day goes by where we don’t think about her.View image in fullscreenSheffield United and Maddy Cusack’s family paid tribute at Bramall Lane shortly after her death.Photograph: Richard Callis/MB Media/Getty Images“There can be days when you just feel absolutely drained and you know you don’t quite know what the right thing to do is, but I think the way that we just get through it is that we remember who she was as a person. She loved her life, she loved trying new things and just enjoying life’s simple pleasures, we try and embody that on every day, not just the anniversary.“I really do encourage people to, as difficult as it can be sometimes, share the photos, share the memories, bring her up in conversation wherever you can, talk about her, and between all of us, you know her legacy will live on.”The family have already endured eight full days of evidence, after the hearing began belatedly on 29 June, but the discovery of additional documents led the proceedings to be paused until December. The coroner apologised to the family for yet another delay. The case had been set previously to start being heard on 5 January 2026 after additional postponements in 2025.“It’s been really difficult,” Olivia said of the delays. “It’s not something that any of us anticipated to happen. It’s very confusing and it can be very frustrating, the length of time it’s taken, it can be difficult to work that out and to know how you should be feeling and the process of it. However, we know that for the right outcome it has to be taken seriously. They need the time to come together and really get an outcome.View image in fullscreenMaddy Cusack was also remembered during the Premier League match between Sheffield United and Newcastle.Photograph: George Wood/Getty Images“It feels as though she can’t be at peace until it’s finished. And I do feel that’s quite upsetting to think about and to work through. It needs to come to a conclusion.”Olivia said she would “channel Maddy’s energy” during the 29-mile walk on Saturday, when a group of about 15 family and friends travelled in the reverse direction to another fundraising walk in February 2024 from Pride Park to Bramall Lane.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThis time they set off from Sheffield at 5.30am. Afundraising pagefor the walk had surpassed £1,100 as of Saturday afternoon. Olivia described that tally as “incredible – £1,000 is just amazing, it’s more than I ever expected” and said: “Particularly with it being Maddy’s anniversary, it’s going to be very much a mental challenge as well as a physical one, so it gives you that extra motivation to make the people who’ve donated proud.”The money is being raised for the Maddy Cusack Foundation, which is helping a range of causes targeting women’s and girls’ football and “letting girls be seen within sport”.“We provided Derby County Community Trust with a series of bursaries for girls and families who struggle with the financial prospects of becoming dedicated to their football. It’s a helping hand for any child that needs that extra sort of funding, taking away the barriers that they might face.”The foundation has also partnered with the Stockport County left wing-back and former Derby, Sheffield United and Nottingham Forest player defender Ben Osborn’s organisation Elite Football Development, which aims to inspire young people through sport and education.“They work with girls and boys but we sponsor the girls’ side of things, which is focused around post-16 study, and allows girls to gain qualifications alongside being able to train and live the life of a professional footballer. We were really keen to get involved in this as Maddy was really passionate about education.”In the UK and Ireland,Samaritanscan be contacted on freephone 116 123.In the US, you can call or text theNational Suicide Prevention Lifelineon 988, chat on988lifeline.org, ortext HOMEto 741741 to connect with a crisis counsellor. In Australia, the crisis support serviceLifelineis 13 11 14. Other international helplines can be found atbefrienders.orgExplore more on these topicsWomen's footballinterviewsShareReuse this content

title: Jonathan David earns Atlético precious win over 10-man Real Madrid in fractious derby | La Liga | The Guardian
description: Atlético Madrid took a 2-0 lead against Real Madrid, who had Dean Huijsen sent off, and survived after Antonio Rüdiger’s late goal, to win 2-1
Author: Sid Lowe
Headline: Atlético Madrid took a 2-0 lead against Real Madrid, who had Dean Huijsen sent off, and survived after Antonio Rüdiger’s late goal, to win 2-1
Content: Jonathan David (left) high-fives Giuliano Simeone after scoring Atlético Madrid’s second goal.Photograph: Juan Barbosa/ReutersView image in fullscreenJonathan David (left) high-fives Giuliano Simeone after scoring Atlético Madrid’s second goal.Photograph: Juan Barbosa/ReutersLa LigaJonathan David earns Atlético precious win over 10-man Real Madrid in fractious derbySid Loweat the Riyadh Air MetropolitanoSun 20 Sep 2026 14.10 EDTLast modified on Sun 20 Sep 2026 19.19 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleOn the eve of the derby, Diego Simeone described this as a special week in Madrid, a “tremendous energy about the city”, and it closed the way he wanted. He had enjoyed the Formula One, he said, and he had enjoyed seeing Shakira in concert, but he enjoyed this even more. At least he did by the time the last of many, many blows on the referee’s whistle brought it to an end, sprinting up the tunnel punching the air. Having been 2-0 up against 10 men through goals from Álex Grimaldo and Jonathan David, seemingly in control, a late header from Antonio Rüdiger awoke old ghosts and brought tension, but they did it.José Mourinho’s first derby back atReal Madridended in defeat and recriminations: he turned up in the press conference with a picture of two moments in which he claimed that Lee Kang-in and Cristian Romero should have been sent off and insisted the story was there. And yet there are other questions: over the way Dean Huijsen gave away the penalty and got the red card that tilted the game against them, and how his team played, how little they did.Carlos Espí gives Real Madrid hope in the face of Barcelona’s La Liga storm | Sid LoweRead moreIt is 13 years since these two managers met in this fixture, their last time the night Atlético won the Cup at the Santiago Bernabéu. Then, Mourinho was sent off and didn’t collect his medal from the king. His return has been driven by nostalgia and it was like old times in the press room. He and Simeone are “companions of war”, he had said, and so it was.It was not until the 39th minute that there was a shot on target when Atlético’s Jan Oblak pushed Arda Guler’s long-range effort away. Otherwise, there was little football but it had been heating up from the beginning, Guler the first to confront the referee after a foul by Álex Baena. To which he responded by fouling Baena back. From the bench, something was said and Diego Simeone was booked; the scene had been set.Atlético probed from wide, almost always the right wing. An advance on that side led to Ibrahima Konaté doubting and Giuliano Simeone flashing wide. At the other end Vinícius Júnior shot over twice before the half’s most significant moment. Which, appropriately, was not about the play.Jude Bellingham slid in to tackle Romero and the referee showed him a yellow. Bellingham, his teammates and the bench were incensed and the video assistant referee was engaged. The referee Miguel Ángel Ortiz, struggling to control this, went to the screen where he saw Romero’s studs hit Bellingham’s knee. The decision was reversed, the Englishman’s yellow taken away and shown to the Argentinian instead. The hosts still felt it should have been red for Bellingham. When Lee’s studs went in on Federico Valverde’s ankle, Real did too. Confrontations continued, words exchanged, but chances didn’t come. At half-time Atlético’s goalkeeper coach and Real’s assistant were sent off.The second half began with Koke introduced and Baena forcing a save. It was Atlético’s first shot on target and the start of a different game. Their second soon after gave them the lead and an advantage that was even bigger. A long ball from David Hancko dropped into the run of Simeone and as he dashed into the area Huijsen dragged him down. Ortiz pointed to the spot. He was also called to the screen again – not to overturn the penalty but to change the colour of the card. Huijsen walked, Grimaldo scored and the Metropolitano exploded.View image in fullscreenReal Madrid’s Dean Huijsen fouls Giuliano Simeone leading to a penalty and a red card for the defender.Photograph: Juan Carlos Lucas/Zuma Press Wire/ShutterstockYou suspected Mourinho would too. First, he removed Guler and Vinícius to introduce Yan Diomandé and Rüdiger. Vinícius had done little and a readjustment was required but there have been times when decisions like this – the Brazilian’s removal in last year’sclásicowas the beginning of the end for Xabi Alonso – have caused splits. It did not improve things either. Instead, Real were oddly passive and Atlético doubled the lead. It came from the right where Lee, outstanding, worked the ball to Simeone. His low cross, bent behind Madrid’s back four, was perfect. Six yards out, David turned it in.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionStill Atlético came. Courtois made an extraordinary save from Romero and Konaté cleared off the line from Julián Alvarez. Real could do nothing, seemingly concerned only with limiting the damage. Oblak barely saw them. Real did not touch the ball in his area until they scored. Kylian Mbappé barely touched the ball anywhere. Inside Atlético’s half, a pigeon pecked the grass, uninterrupted.When Diomandé did at last dash into that space with 15 minutes to go, Oblak saved, the opportunity to make a match of this wasted. Or so it seemed until, from a dead ball that was too late even for them, Rüdiger headed in to spark a rebellion that would prove brief and incomplete, unlike Simeone’s week.Explore more on these topicsLa LigaAtlético MadridReal MadridEuropean club footballmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: McCullum hails Brook’s captaincy as England move top of T20 world rankings | England cricket team | The Guardian
description: McCullum says that Brook has ‘grown as captain and as a person’ as England prepare for their ODI series against Sri Lanka this week
Author: Tanya Aldred
Headline: McCullum says that Brook has ‘grown as captain and as a person’ as England prepare for their ODI series against Sri Lanka this week
Content: Harry Brook (centre) chats with Brendon McCullum (left) after England completed a 3-0 T20 series clean sweep over Sri Lanka.Photograph: Martin Rickett/PAView image in fullscreenHarry Brook (centre) chats with Brendon McCullum (left) after England completed a 3-0 T20 series clean sweep over Sri Lanka.Photograph: Martin Rickett/PAEngland cricket teamMcCullum hails Brook’s captaincy as England move top of T20 world rankingsMcCullum: Brook has ‘grown as captain and person’England begin ODI series against Sri Lanka this weekTanya AldredSun 20 Sep 2026 13.11 EDTLast modified on Sun 20 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleEngland’s white-ball coach, Brendon McCullum, was full of praise for the captain, Harry Brook, after Saturday’seight-wicket victoryover Sri Lanka completed a T20 series whitewash and took the side to No 1 in the world.Brook, player of the T20 series against Sri Lanka, has now won 23 of his 26 completed games as captain. If he is not yet considered a suitable candidate as Test leader, the cap fits nicely in the smash and grab format.‘I can’t wait for the Ashes’: new Test coach Fleming wants England to be No 1Read more“He’s grown not just as captain, but as a person as well,” said McCullum. “He seems very comfortable now as a leader of this side and the guys follow him, they trust him. Obviously his batting’s been on a different planet when it comes to T20 cricket, but I think his ability to do things differently based on what’s required with the conditions, and also against the opposition, has been probably the most impressive element.“Twenty20 is such an inconsistent game, so you can never take your eye off what you’re trying to achieve, but over the last 18 months or so we’ve found a nice level of consistency. We are not the finished article as yet, but the work we’ve done on the environment and the setup, and the depth that we’ve got in our side now is certainly encouraging.”Quick GuideMiddlesex win One-Day Cup to end white-ball waitShowRyan Higgins [pictured] made a fine 100 and then took the key catch to dismiss fellow centurion Nick Kelly as Middlesex beat Leicestershire by 31 runs to win the Metro Bank One-Day Cup final at Trent Bridge.Higgins’ first List A century and a 135-run sixth wicket partnership with Harry Duke (55) had earlier helped turn Middlesex’s innings around from 71 for five to 231 all out. After Leicestershire slipped to 79 for five, Kelly dug in with a determined 103 of his own.Once Kelly had been caught by Higgins at mid-wicket off Tom Helm with nine overs left, Middlesex picked up the final two Leicestershire wickets to secure a first trophy since their 2016 Championship triumph, and first men's white-ball trophy since winning the Twenty20 Cup in 2008.Higgins was out for 100, which came from 114 balls, and included nine fours, at the start of Middlesex’s 49th over, caught by Kelly when trying to go over long-on off Ian Holland. Leicestershire wicketkeeper Ben Cox took five consecutive catches while Holland claimed five for 36 and Rehan Ahmed three for 55.After the Leicestershire captain, Stephen Eskinazi (12), was out at the start of the sixth over, the Foxes continued to lose wickets as Toby Roland-Jones took three for 27 in his 10-over spell. Kelly then steadied the innings alongside Holland to push Leicestershire’s reply on to 110 at the halfway stage.The partnership was finally broken in the 29th over when Holland (15) was stumped off Zafar Gohar. Kelly brought up his century at the start of the 41st over, coming off 103 balls with 10 fours and three sixes before his resistance was finally broken.PA MediaPhotograph: Mike Egerton/PAWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Alongside his relationship with Brook, there is a new guy in town to manage – McCullum’s old buddy and the new Test coach, Stephen ­Fleming, who was also at Old Trafford on Saturday.“Flem and I are great mates,” said McCullum. “He was my captain coming through and the great thing about him is he always made you feel like his equal. Our relationship is brilliant and fundamentally we both just want what is right for English cricket and will do whatever we can across the formats to make cricket as good as we can in the time that we’re here. I think our relationship is a real strength, we talk regularly regardless of these jobs.”View image in fullscreenHarry Brook flicks a shot away en route to his 33-run tally against Sri Lanka on Saturday.Photograph: Roger Evans/Action Plus/ShutterstockAnd he was confident that their relationship would ensure there was no conflict when there is a clash between Test and white-ball commitments. McCullum even drew Fleming into the England huddle before Saturday’s game. “He was a bit reluctant but it’s brilliant to have him around. He’s one of the most successful T20 coaches in the world, so it is quite handy to have him run his eye over the environment.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe SpinSubscribe to our cricket newsletter for our writers' thoughts on the biggest stories and a review of the week’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionEngland begin a three-match ODI series against Sri Lanka on Tuesday. McCullum had warm words about Sonny Baker, whose control and pace has been a revelation. “He bowls 90mph, has a good slower ball, can swing the ball both ways and is an incredible competitor. He has been tested in international cricket and probably didn’t get the instant results he wanted but he’ll be walking a foot taller now and that’s great for all of us whether that’s T20 cricket, one-day cricket, or Test cricket. People like him are rare commodities.”Towards the other end of his England career is Adil Rashid, who will be 40 by the time the next T20 World Cup comes around in 2028.“We hope Rash is around for a long time. He’s a world-class performer but we do have to have plans in place. We have guys we are keeping an eye on consistently, obviously Rehan Ahmed has been around our squad a lot and he’s never let us down, there are lots of other guys out there as well. The one-dayers could be an opportunity to have a look.”Explore more on these topicsEngland cricket teamBrendon McCullumHarry BrookCricketSri Lanka cricket teamnewsShareReuse this content

title: Evenepoel wins fourth world time trial title in a row, Reusser retains her crown | Cycling | The Guardian
description: Belgium’s Remco Evenepoel won the men’s time trial title for the fourth time in a row, while the Swiss rider Marlen Reusser defended her women’s crown
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Belgium’s Remco Evenepoel won the men’s time trial title for the fourth time in a row, while the Swiss rider Marlen Reusser defended her women’s crown
Content: Remco Evenepoel celebrates his fourth successive world time trial title after dominating in Montreal.Photograph: Jasper Jacobs/Belga/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenRemco Evenepoel celebrates his fourth successive world time trial title after dominating in Montreal.Photograph: Jasper Jacobs/Belga/ShutterstockCyclingEvenepoel wins fourth world time trial title in a row, Reusser retains her crownRemco Evenepoel dominates men’s event in MontrealMarlen Reusser denies Zoe Backstedt in women’s raceAgence France-PresseSun 20 Sep 2026 16.28 EDTFirst published on Sun 20 Sep 2026 13.16 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRemco Evenepoel etched his name into the history books with a dominant fourth successive men’s world time-trial victory in Montreal on Sunday.The 2024 Olympic champion came into the race as the overwhelming favourite and he did not disappoint. Evenepoel was already more than 30 seconds ahead of the rest by the second intermediate time check, just over halfway along the 39.2km (24.4 mile) route.Sports quiz of the week: records, hazards, complaints and boring eventsRead moreBy the time he reached the finish line, the 26-year-old Belgian had put almost a minute into second-placed Filippo Ganna of Italy, with the French rider Paul Seixas taking third another 15 seconds back. Evenepoel has not lost a time trial since the 2025 Tour de France.Evenepoel becomes the first man to win the time trial world title four times in a row, while also equalling the record number of overall titles held by Germany’s Tony Martin and the Swiss rider Fabian Cancellara.He has enjoyed his best season to date so far this year, winning the Amstel Gold Race, Clásica San Sebastián and Grand Prix de Québec, as well as finishing second behind Tadej Pogacar this year at the Tour de France.Ganna started slowly and was only 10th at the first time check, but by the third he had moved up into second spot. But he could not make any headway into Evenepoel, who did not stop increasing his lead from the start to the finish.The young Swedish rider Jakob Soderqvist, the under-23 champion in this discipline last year, was second to Evenepoel at the first two time checks but faded over the last 10km and finished fifth. The teenager Seixas gauged his effort better and put in a strong ride over the final 10km to finish third.Earlier on Sunday, Marlen Reusser retained her world time-trial title as her expected main challenger, Demi Vollering, finished a disappointing eighth.Reusser secured an ultimately comfortable victory in Montreal, winning her second world championship after triumphing last year in Kigali – but not before the young British rider Zoe Backstedt gave her a scare.Backstedt had been quickest at the first two intermediate time checks on the course but Reusser powered away in the second half of the race to beat the 21-year-old by 40sec. Germany’s Franziska Koch finished third, a further 6sec back.View image in fullscreenMarlen Reusser (centre) receives her gold medal with Zoe Backstedt (left) winning silver and Franziska Koch (right) bronze.Photograph: Chris Auld/SWpix.com/Shutterstock“It’s a good present,” said Reusser, who was competing on her 35th birthday. “I also thought, win or not, I have something to celebrate.“From the side of pacing and understanding how fast you should go and how you should also cope with these challenges on the way, I was really nervous. I was not really sure, because we don’t have time trials like this often … I’m used to doing 20km.”Reusser has been virtually unbeatable in races against the clock in the past few years. The Swiss cyclist is a four-time European champion and has won time-trial stages at the Tour de France Femmes and Giro d’Italia Women.Backstedt had been a junior and twice under-23 world champion in the discipline, but this race was around 12km further than any previous time trial in which she had competed. Koch’s bronze medal continued a dream season for the German, who won Paris-Roubaix in April. Vollering, the European road race champion, was never in the running for a medal.Elsewhere,Mathieu van der Poelwarmed up for his bid for a second world road rice title with a long-range solo break on the final stage of the Tour of Luxembourg .The Dutch star broke clear just over a couple of kilometres into the 177km stage and held on in front all day to win by more than a minute. Van der Poel’s run is thought to be one of the longest solo breaks in the history of cycling.The 2023 world road race champion will be one of the favourites in Montreal next weekend, where the reigning champion Pogacar will be missing because of injury.“That was not the plan before the start, but I found myself alone from the start of the race in fact, and I just rode my tempo the whole day,” Van der Poel said. Italy’s Davide Piganzoli finished fourth on the stage to secure overall victory.Explore more on these topicsCyclingUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Patten and Skupski take Great Britain past Ecuador to reach Davis Cup Final 8 | Davis Cup | The Guardian
description: Henry Patten and Neal Skupski won their doubles match in straight sets to put Great Britain into the Final 8 in Bologna in November
Author: Tumaini Carayol
Headline: Henry Patten and Neal Skupski won their doubles match in straight sets to put Great Britain into the Final 8 in Bologna in November
Content: Henry Patten (right) and Neal Skupski celebrate with their captain, Leon Smith (centre), after sealing the 3-0 win.Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenHenry Patten (right) and Neal Skupski celebrate with their captain, Leon Smith (centre), after sealing the 3-0 win.Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/ReutersDavis CupPatten and Skupski take Great Britain past Ecuador to reach Davis Cup Final 8GB pair win doubles match in straight setsFinals to be played in Bologna in NovemberTumaini Carayolat the Copper BoxSun 20 Sep 2026 09.41 EDTLast modified on Sun 20 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFew people across London enjoyed a more soothing night’s sleep than Leon Smith on Saturday. After an ideal first day for his team in theirDavis Cupqualifier against Ecuador, where his singles players handled business efficiently, the Great Britain captain had the luxury of calling upon one member of each of the two best doubles pairs in the world to close out the tie.In just their second match as partners rather than rivals the world No 1, Henry Patten, and Neal Skupski, the US Open champion a week ago, played their roles to perfection as they convincingly sealed their place in the Davis Cup Final 8 with a clinical 6-3, 6-4 victory against Gonzalo Escobar and Diego Hidalgo, securing for Great Britain an unassailable 3-0 lead. Harry Wendelken, the British No 7, closed out the tie with a 6-2, 6-3 win against Angel Veliz in the dead rubber.GB take command of Ecuador Davis Cup tie on Arthur Fery’s London returnRead moreThe British team will next head to Bologna for the quarter-final knockout stage of the competition, which takes place between 24 and 29 November in the final week of the tennis season, for the first time since 2023. Their success in east London was dictated by wins on Saturday byArthur Fery, the British No 1, and the No 5, Toby Samuel, who overcame tense starts before settling down and easing to victory.“There’s obviously a lot of tennis to be played before [the Davis Cup Finals], but it’s really a great thing to look forward to,” Smith said. “I’m really pleased how each of the players have gone about things in different ways yesterday and today. I think starting today, it’s a real privilege to have Henry and Neil at the top of the game. And just like we talked about in the singles, upsets happen, but they didn’t let it happen. The way they prepare, their quality, their competitiveness. I thought they were excellent.”Smith had warned on Saturday evening that there would probably be few breaks in the doubles match because of the fast indoor conditions inside the Copper Box. It was a source of great pleasure, then, when Patten and Skupski burst into the match with a brilliant opening return game, immediately breaking serve with no fewer than three lob winners, including a particularly sweet backhand from Skupski on break point.The British pair did not face a break point in the match, finally breaking serve at 4-4 in the second set from a brilliant forehand return winner by Skupski. “Very happy to play with Henry,” Skupski said, smiling. “It’s a privilege to play with the world No 1.”Patten responded to the compliment by rolling his eyes, drawing laughter from Skupski and Smith: “It’s a privilege for me to play with the US Open champion as well. Former world No 1.”This has been a good weekend for the Davis Cup, with ties around the world attracting strong crowds and great atmospheres, including the sold-out Copper Box. This was undoubtedly a great draw for the British team – in the best tie of the weekend, the USA team were toppled 3-2 by an excellent Czech squad before 13,000 fans each day in Prague, while France fell against Canada in front of 10,000 Québecois fans led by Félix Auger-Aliassime – but this is still a good result.It is also a good reflection of the Great Britain team’s overall depth, with five British players now inside the singles top 100. They were still able to succeed in the absence of their two most successful active singles players. While Jack Draper has been sidelined for an extended period, Cameron Norrie could only passionately cheer on from the sidelines during the past week after he was forced to withdraw at the last minute because of injury.The draw for the final eight will be made on Tuesday. With Germany, Austria, South Korea, Czechia, Canada and the home nation Italy all qualified, and Spain likely to take the final spot, Britain’s next opponent will probably present a far greater challenge. “If everyone’s fit and healthy, we’re going to have some difficult choices to make as well,” Smith said. “But it’ll be tough.“You’ve seen the players that have played this weekend for the [other] nations and others will, I presume, come in, whether that’s [Jannik] Sinner or [Carlos] Alcaraz, if they make it. So it’s going to be tough, but that’s exactly why you want to be in the final eight. You want that excitement.”Explore more on these topicsDavis CupArthur FeryTennisnewsShareReuse this content

title: Deaths of three women in sea at Brighton had no criminal involvement, police say | Brighton | The Guardian
description: Jane Adetoro, Christina Walters and Rebecca Walters from Uxbridge were found on 13 May
Author: Charlie Moloney
Headline: Jane Adetoro, Christina Walters and Rebecca Walters from Uxbridge were found on 13 May
Content: L-R: Jane Adetoro, Joseph Jacobson, Christina Walters and Rebecca Walters, in an old family photo.Photograph: Sussex PoliceView image in fullscreenL-R: Jane Adetoro, Joseph Jacobson, Christina Walters and Rebecca Walters, in an old family photo.Photograph: Sussex PoliceBrightonDeaths of three women in sea at Brighton had no criminal involvement, police sayJane Adetoro, Christina Walters and Rebecca Walters from Uxbridge were found on 13 MayCharlie MoloneySun 20 Sep 2026 15.03 EDTLast modified on Sun 20 Sep 2026 15.10 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe deaths of three sisters found in the sea offBrightonbeach did not involve any criminality or third-party involvement, police have concluded.The bodies of Jane Adetoro, 36, Christina Walters, 32, and Rebecca Walters, 31, from Uxbridge, west London,were foundon 13 May. A postmortem conducted that month confirmed all three women died by drowning.Specialist detectives worked to trace the sisters’ final movements and understand how they came to be in the water that morning, Sussex police said.The investigation found all three women were dropped off by taxi at Madeira Drive, the road running along Brighton Beach, at 10.20pm on 12 May, wearing everyday clothing.No evidence was found to suggest they visited any nightclubs or local businesses in the area at the time and the investigation concluded all three women entered the water near to where their bodies were found, the police spokesperson added.A spokesperson for the force said: “The purpose of the police investigation was to identify any evidence of criminal offending linked to how the sisters came to be in the water or their subsequent deaths.“We can confirm the thorough police investigation has not found any evidence of a crime being committed or involvement by a third party.”Additional details such as the sisters’ specific movements before their deaths and their potential reasons for entering the water will be considered during the East Sussex coroner’s inquest.Ch Supt Adam Hays said his force had been “acutely aware of the speculation surrounding this incident” and “concerns raised by black communities surrounding the deaths of black people in or near bodies of water”.He said: “Jane, Rebecca and Christina’s tragic deaths sparked a national outpouring of grief, and I would like to thank everyone who supported our investigation by coming forward with information. We will now support the coronial process and ask that the sisters’ family continue to be given privacy to come to terms with their loss.”After the sisters’ deaths, their father, Joseph Jacobson, said there were days when the grief felt unbearable but that he held on to the memories they had shared and “the bond that death can never take away”.In a statement released through Sussex police, Jacobson said: “Jane, Christina and Becky were more than daughters to me: they were my joy, my strength and the beautiful light that filled our family with happiness and love.“Each of you was unique and precious in your own special way. Your smiles brightened dark days, your laughter brought comfort and your presence made life more meaningful. Though your time on Earth was short, the impact you made will remain in our hearts for ever.”A GoFundMe online fundraiser for the women’s funerals has received more than 2,200 donations from members of the public, totalling nearly £46,000.Explore more on these topicsBrightonnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘An out-of-touch Silicon Valley radical’: meet Trump’s AI whisperer pushing for limited regulation | Trump administration | The Guardian
description: David Sacks convinced Trump against any restrictions on AI – putting the White House out of step with its own party
Author: Dara Kerr
Headline: David Sacks convinced Trump against any restrictions on AI – putting the White House out of step with its own party
Content: David Sacks, CEO of Zenefits, speaks during 2016 TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco, California, on 13 September 2016.Photograph: Beck Diefenbach/ReutersView image in fullscreenDavid Sacks, CEO of Zenefits, speaks during 2016 TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco, California, on 13 September 2016.Photograph: Beck Diefenbach/ReutersTrump administrationProfile‘An out-of-touch Silicon Valley radical’: meet Trump’s AI whisperer pushing for limited regulationDavid Sacks convinced Trump against any restrictions on AI – putting the White House out of step with its own partyDara KerrSun 20 Sep 2026 12.44 EDTFirst published on Sun 20 Sep 2026 09.00 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAs lawmakers from both sides of the aisle in the US have joined together calling for the regulation of powerfulartificial intelligencemodels, one of the few vocal naysayers has beenDonald Trump. He’s called the perceived dangers of the technology a “hoax” and a “scam”, arguing that the government already has “tremendous CRIMINAL and REGULATORY power over these companies”.It’s a starkly different stance from those of his former adviserSteve Bannon, the Republican Texas senatorTed Cruzand even the heads of the world’s leading AI companies. But it’s directly in line with the opinion of David Sacks – a prominent billionaire venture capitalist and Trump’s onetime AI and crypto czar, who has pushed back publicly and forcefully against recent claims of an impending AI apocalypse.China bogeyman looms large over American firms’ AI doomsday scenarioRead moreSacks, who believes regulation will erase the US lead in the global AI race, is seen as Trump’s AI whisperer – the adviser with the greatest influence in the White House on the topic. Time and again, he’s counseled the president to give a soft touch to AI regulation, helping push executive orders and other measures aimed at loosening restrictions on the technology. He also maintains direct financial stakes in multiple AI companies.On Friday, more than 100 AI researchers, professors and technologistssigned a public letterurging third-party evaluations of AI models and outlining how that should be done. The signatories included some of the most notable experts in the field, such as Geoffrey Hinton, the “godfather of AI”, and Stuart Russell, a renowned AI computer scientist.Sacks, in characteristic form, dismissed the letteron social media, calling third-party evaluations “pseudoscience” and “censorship and control”.“The last time we had media-generated panics like this (with Russiagate and Covid), social media companies created ‘trust & safety’ teams to censor conservative and dissident voices,” Sacks wrote. “These groups haven’t earned our trust, and their agenda is not our safety.”The next day, Trump proclaimed he would soon create an “AI Force” headed by an AI czar, Sacks’ previous title. It’s not clear if the venture capitalist will assume the mantle again, but he was quick torespond on X, praising Trump’s efforts and deriding a potential pause on AI once again.Derailing AI safety effortsLast December, Trump signed anexecutive orderto halt state laws that limited AI. It was one of the first of several actions by the president that put his alignment with Sacks on full display. The proclamation assigned a federal taskforce to have the “sole responsibility” of challenging states that attempt to pass laws restricting the technology. The order spelled out aninfluential role for Sacksto direct the taskforce’s litigation against states.Then, just four months later, in March, the White Houseunveiled an AI policy for Congressthat encouraged lawmakers to pre-empt state rules. Again, Sacks was seen asworking behind the scenesto make this happen. This pattern has continued throughout the year. In July, Trump and Sackshosted a fanfare-filled AI summitin Washington.And just this week, Trump called Nvidia’s CEO, Jensen Huang, to discuss AI regulation. In a live demonstration of Sacks’ proximity to the most powerful people in the US, the call came in while Sacks was interviewing Huang at an event on stage.Next week, Trump is hosting China’s leader, Xi Jinping, at the White House and is expected to invite several AI CEOs to be present. Sacks is also slated to be one of the guests in attendance,according to NBC News.Isabel Sunderland, the policy lead for technology reform at the non-profit Issue One, said that Sacks’ relationship with the president shows what happens when money can buy a direct line to power.“David Sacks advising President Trump on AI shows exactly how our political system serves the wealthy and well-connected instead of everyday Americans,” Sunderland said. “This is about more than just AI regulation – it’s about who’s allowed to write the rules.”Trump’s most recent full-throated opposition to AI regulation comes after an Anthropic employee, Jacob Coxon, announced on social media last week that he wasresigning from the company, saying AI would soon become “superhuman systems” that could cause human extinction by 2030. After Coxon’s post, other Anthropic employees backed these predictions, with one saying: “We really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans!”The end-of-the-world prognostications whipped up a frenzy of media and lawmakers’ attention over the past two weeks, with US politicians, heads of state and international bodies calling for the tech to be reined in.Dario Amodei, the CEO of Anthropic,issued a proposalto slow down the technology’s advancement and ensure public safety by regulating the industry. In a rare public display of unity, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Google DeepMind chief Demis Hassabis and xAI owner Elon Musk agreed.Sacks, however, pushed back on any regulatory action, instead indicating the proposal was an “election-season psyop” and a bid for “regulatory capture”.In a lengthy social mediapostresponding to Amodei’s proposal, Sacks said: “If the unreleased models are scary enough that you think you should slow down, I support your decision to be responsible. But stop pretending you need anyone else’s permission.”Sacks’ political evolutionSacks, like his tech contemporaries Elon Musk and Peter Thiel, hails from South Africa. He was born in Cape Town in 1972 and then emigrated with his family to the US in the late 1970s. Sacks spent his college career majoring in economics at Stanford, where he met Thiel and worked with him at the conservative student-run newspaper the Stanford Review.The two men also collaborated after graduating, co-authoring in 1995 the book The Diversity Myth: Multiculturalism and the Politics of Intolerance at Stanford, an early glimpse into Sacks’ political ideology. The book rails against “multiculturalism”, “diversity” and the “politically correct” decline of higher education.By the late 90s and early 2000s, Sacks, Thiel, Musk and others worked together at PayPal, becoming members of what’s now known as the PayPal Mafia – an elite group of influential and wealthy tech investors and founders.After founding and working at various startups over the years, Sacks co-founded Craft Ventures in 2017. The fund has raised hundreds of millions for tech companies and has investments in an array of businesses, including SpaceX, Anduril, Palantir, Meta, Airbnb, Lyft and dozens of AI startups. As of 2023, Sacks said the firm’s assets under managementtotaled $3.3bn.Around the same time as founding Craft Ventures, Sacks started to get more into politics. While he donated toHillary Clinton’s 2016 bid for president, he quickly pivoted to backing mostly Republican candidates and causes.In March 2020, Sacks launched the popular and influential All-In tech podcast with three other Silicon Valley investors who lean conservative and trumpet capitalist values. Vanity Fairprofiled their annual All-In summitin 2025, calling the gathering a “fever-dream capitalist bacchanal where the faithful can stop being ‘guilt-tripped by this woke mind virus’ and get into ‘founder mode’”.Since then, Sacks’ rightward stances and political giving have deepened, according to aprofile in the Atlantic. He donated to JD Vance, Blake Masters, Ron DeSantis and Robert F Kennedy Jr, campaign finance filings show. In June 2024, Sacksthrew a fundraiser for Trumpat his $45m French-limestone mansion in San Francisco’s Pacific Heights. Tickets went for $500,000 per couple.“President Trump is relaxed, happy, and cracking jokes about AI,” Harmeet Dhillon, assistant attorney general at Trump’s Department of Justice,postedon social media from the event.The AI czar’s time in the White HouseAfter Trump won the presidency, he named Sacks his AI and crypto czar, a newly created role.The position, as a “special government employee”, only allowed Sacks to work for the administration for a maximum of 130 days a year, but exempted him from confirmation hearings or financial disclosure requirements. The office of government ethics did require Craft Ventures to divest in some of its AI holdings, though.In March, Sacks said he was leaving the position, but he’s since maintained close ties with the president. In May, he successfullyurged Trump to scrap an executive orderthat would’ve subjected AI models to government review. And in July, the two men hosted the AI summit in Washington. At the event, the president delivered an “AI action plan”, once again aimed at relaxing restrictions on the development and deployment of the technology.Sacks’ influence on Trump has rankled other senior administration officials, according to theWall Street Journal. Scott Bessent and Susie Wiles have both voiced concerns about the effects of AI on the country and have advised Trump to mandate increased oversight on the technology. But the president has consistently sided with Sacks on the issue.Critics say that Trump and Sacks are out of step with the American public on safeguarding AI, even amongRepublicans. A May poll by Bryson Gillette Insights for the AI safety group Future of Life Institute, found that 85% of Republicans say they support Trump taking strong action to ensure AI is developed and deployed safely.“Running the David Sacks playbook on AI might be the biggest miscalculation theTrump administrationhas made,” Sacha Haworth, the executive director of the Tech Oversight Project, said. “He is an out-of-touch Silicon Valley radical who wants to replace humans with machines. You cannot put this guy in charge and not expect to pay a political price. Republicans are going to follow big tech executives right over a cliff.”Sacks and the White House did not respond to requests for comment.Explore more on these topicsTrump administrationAI (artificial intelligence)Donald TrumpRepublicansUS politicsprofilesShareReuse this content

title: More than a dozen arrested in connection with 2021 assassination of Haitian president | Haiti | The Guardian
description: Jovenel Moïse, 53, was shot dead in July 2021 in a killing which sparked chaos in Haiti
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Jovenel Moïse, 53, was shot dead in July 2021 in a killing which sparked chaos in Haiti
Content: Haiti's president Jovenel Moïse speaks during a press conference in March 2020.Photograph: Andrés Martínez Casares/ReutersView image in fullscreenHaiti's president Jovenel Moïse speaks during a press conference in March 2020.Photograph: Andrés Martínez Casares/ReutersHaitiMore than a dozen arrested in connection with 2021 assassination of Haitian presidentJovenel Moïse, 53, was shot dead in July 2021 in a killing which sparked chaos in HaitiAgence France-PresseSun 20 Sep 2026 16.17 EDTLast modified on Sun 20 Sep 2026 17.24 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleEighteen people have been arrested in association with the 2021 assassination of the Haitian president Jovenel Moïse, according to US officials.Moïse, 53, was shot dead on 7 July 2021 at his private residence by a hired group of about 20 military-trained Colombian mercenaries. His security detail did not intervene to protect him.“Today’s multi-location and international arrests underscore the FBI’s continued commitment to bringing all participants in this plot to justice,” FBI special agent Brett Skiles said on Sunday.The suspects have been taken to Florida to stand trial.In the same post on X, federal prosecutor Jason Reding Quinones said: “18 transported in military plane from Haiti to face American justice in the southern district of Florida.”“Five years later, we are still bringing defendants before American courts, and we are not finished,” Quinones wrote, adding that 30 suspects have thus far been indicted in the killing.In May, four men were convicted in a federal court in Miami of charges including conspiracy to kill or kidnap Moïse, conspiracy to provide material support and violating the US Neutrality Act to engage in an illicit military operation abroad.The men face possible sentences of life in prison.All four were linked to CTU, a private security firm based in Florida, and lured into the plot by the prospect of securing lucrative contracts in the event of Moïse’s ouster, according to federal prosecutors.Eleven people have already been indicted in connection with the assassination in US courts, which have jurisdiction over plots hatched on American soil.Five of them have been sentenced to life in prison, including a former Colombian soldier, a former Haitian senator, a Haitian Chilean businessman, a retired Colombian soldier and a Haitian American.Haiti has descended into deeper chaos since Moïse’s killing, and currently has no president.It is preparing to hold its first presidential and legislative election since 2016, as well as a referendum on the constitution, on 13 December – if security conditions allow.Gangs control about 80% of Port-au-Prince, and violent crimes such as kidnappings for ransom, armed robbery and carjackings plague the impoverished nation.A UN-backed armed force tasked with helping local police combat gangs will not be fully staffed by October as planned, its spokesperson said earlier this month.Announced by the UN security council last year, the Gang Suppression Force was expected to ramp up between April and October to a planned capacity of 5,500 uniformed personnel and 50 civilian staff.As of July, it comprised fewer than 1,000 personnel from Chad, Mongolia, Jamaica, Guatemala, El Salvador and Sri Lanka. More recent figures have not been disclosed.Explore more on these topicsHaitiAmericasCaribbeannewsShareReuse this content

title: Trump claims triumphal arch will serve as a ‘top grade military complex’ to store weapons | Donald Trump | The Guardian
description: US president on Truth Social claims his new plan for the 250ft arch comes at the ‘strong request’ of the US military
Author: Ed Pilkington
Headline: US president on Truth Social claims his new plan for the 250ft arch comes at the ‘strong request’ of the US military
Content: Donald Trump holds models of an arch monument during a ballroom dinner in the East Room at the White House in Washington DC on 15 October 2025.Photograph: Jonathan Ernst/ReutersView image in fullscreenDonald Trump holds models of an arch monument during a ballroom dinner in the East Room at the White House in Washington DC on 15 October 2025.Photograph: Jonathan Ernst/ReutersDonald TrumpTrump claims triumphal arch will serve as a ‘top grade military complex’ to store weaponsUS president on Truth Social claims his new plan for the 250ft arch comes at the ‘strong request’ of the US militaryEd Pilkingtonin New YorkSun 20 Sep 2026 09.26 EDTLast modified on Sun 20 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleDonald Trump is proffering a new argument for building his triumphal arch in Washington DC: it will be converted into a “top grade military complex” replete with drone and ammunition storage space and customised sniper facilities on the roof and plaza.In a post on hisTruth Socialplatform on Sunday morning, Trump claimed that his new plan came at the “strong request” of the US military. He said the 250ft structure would be able to “house, store, and have the rapid ability to use large quantities of sniper ammunition in storage”.With the hyperbole that is his trademark, the president added that the arch would be unique. “There will be no facility like this anywhere in the world.”Trump arch could have ‘adverse effects’ on nearby monuments but will proceed, report saysRead moreThe triumphal arch project has come under widespread criticism for its potential impact on the historic area of downtown Washington DC. Its intended location in a circle close to the Memorial Bridge could interrupt the sight lines of several of the most resonant structures, including the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery which would flank it.The siting of the structure close to the Ronald Reagan Washington international airport has also prompted questions from Democratic Congress members.Last week, theNational Park Servicewarned that it could have “adverse effects to historic properties” and called for additional planning before the building work went ahead.The arch is one of several construction projects that Trump has initiated which he claims are necessary to elevate the visual greatness of the US capital but which critics have slammed as thinly veiled efforts to promote his own legacy. They include the creation of a White House ballroom, the refurbishment of the reflecting pool at the Lincoln Memorial and the renovation of the Kennedy Center.All those projects have run into big problems, ranging from criticism of their aesthetic qualities, structural difficulties and legal challenges. In the case of the John F Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, one of the world’s pre-eminent cultural venues, Trump has hinted that he mightdemolish the propertyaltogether in a fit of pique at the courts blocking the addition of his name to its title.The White House ballroom, which Trump has also been calling a “military complex”, was beset by legal wrangling until theUS supreme courtlast month said the project could go ahead.The ground breaking that will kick off construction of the arch is expected to begin this month. Trump has linked it to the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence, and said in Sunday’s post that it would be “by far the greatest” triumphal arch in any of the world’s top cities and capitals.It will be clad in granite, with three golden statues on top.Explore more on these topicsDonald TrumpWashington DCUS militaryTrump administrationnewsShareReuse this content

title: Bear-y good neighbors: humans and animals are learning to live together in an expanding LA | Los Angeles | The Guardian
description: People are increasingly crossing paths with the wild animals as homes ring the outskirts of forests, sparking a new era of coexistence
Author: Nick Visser
Headline: People are increasingly crossing paths with the wild animals as homes ring the outskirts of forests, sparking a new era of coexistence
Content: As communities on the outskirts of LA grow, bears are being drawn to residents’ pools, chicken coops, fruit trees and trashcans.Photograph: Poolbearlife via InstagramView image in fullscreenAs communities on the outskirts of LA grow, bears are being drawn to residents’ pools, chicken coops, fruit trees and trashcans.Photograph: Poolbearlife via InstagramLos AngelesBear-y good neighbors: humans and animals are learning to live together in an expanding LAPeople are increasingly crossing paths with the wild animals as homes ring the outskirts of forests, sparking a new era of coexistenceNick VisserSun 20 Sep 2026 10.00 EDTLast modified on Sun 20 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleEvery year, as summer draws to a close and fall begins, California’s bears get hungry.Black bears have long roamed the state, hunting for acorns, ants and pine nuts by the bucketload to pack on calories before hibernation. But increasingly, for every berry and root, there’s an even greater temptation: our trash and the detritus of human existence.That dynamic is playing out in perhaps a surprising place:Los Angeles. As communities on the outskirts of the metropolis grow, bears are butting up against humanity, drawn to residents’ pools, their chicken coops, their fruit trees and trashcans.“Black bears are incredibly adaptable, versatile omnivores,” said Wilson Sherman, a PhD student at the University of California, Los Angeles, who studies human-wildlife interaction. “They can eat everything we can eat.”View image in fullscreenVideos show bear cubs with their snouts bubbling in the water, climbing – and falling from – trees.Photograph: Poolbearlife via InstagramHuman-bear interactions have increased since the 1990s, Sherman said, which makes sense as communities expand and the state is now home to some 50,000 to 70,000 black bears. A few hundred of those live in the Angeles national forest, just north of the city and its millions of hungry households.Brian Gordon and his partner moved to the state’s bear capital – Monrovia, California – four years ago. Their house is the last before the Angeles national forest begins, and as they were buying the home, a family of bears wandered through the back garden. It was the start of a new era of coexistence.Family of bears play in swimming poolNow, the pair regularly share their pool with a family of bears and document their exploits on an Instagram account called PoolBearLife. Videos show bear cubs with their snouts bubbling in the water, climbing – and falling from – trees and causing adorable, young bear mayhem.“I only had education up until I bought this house of bears from whatever I saw online. I actually thought people get eaten by bears a lot,” Gordon said. “But after we bought the house, we had bears walking through. That’s really all they’re doing. I realized, OK, I have an unnatural fear of these animals and we’ve kind of adapted to living around them.Experience: we found a bear swimming in our poolRead more“People will say ‘you guys are the bear experts,’” Gordon went on. “No, we’re city boys. We bought a house that happened to have bears.”Gordon and his partner live amongst the bears, but they’re also vocal advocates for doing so safely. Trashcans are kept clean, temptations are removed and, despite the filming, they give the bears their space. Sometimes mistakes are made and a bearfinds a case of beerin the garage.But with consideration, bears don’t even stop to sniff the trash cans and will just pass through the backyard like it’s an extension of the forest nearby, the couple said.In a perfect world, Sherman said, human dominated landscapes that buttress the natural world would take steps to minimize bear contact. That means making neighborhoods as unattractive to bears as possible.“Pet food left outside, koi ponds, fruit trees with a lot of fruit on them, swimming pools, all these things can be attractive to bears,” he said.It’s not that human food tastes better, it’s just much more calorie dense and therefore easier for bears to pack on the pounds. In fact, bears that live or forage near human environments tend to reproduce more often and at higher rates, likely due to the availability of our food.“It takes a lot of work to get the calories from, say, a half eaten pizza in the trash in equivalent calories from acorns and ants,” he said. “It makes sense to get calories from human food.”The other major factor is climate crisis. Warmer summers can alter the availability of natural food and force bears to expand their ranges. Major wildfires like the 2025 Eaton and Palisades fires were also linked to a lack in natural food sources, prompting the bears near Los Angeles to search in neighborhoods instead.View image in fullscreenAs September draws to a close, interactions between bears and Angelenos will thin out for the season.Photograph: Poolbearlife via InstagramAlex Heeran, a research scientist at the California department of fish and wildlife who studies the human dimensions of wildlife encounters, said human and bear interactions generally peak every year in late summer and early fall. September is often a really active month as black bears finish up their pre-hibernation hungry period, known as hyperphagia. 2026 is on track to be a record-setting year when it comes to reported bear encounters, Heeran said.It’s also a time when humans are out in force around Labor Day for the year’s final picnics and camping excursions. Fish and wildlife officials will often get reports of bears creating a nuisance and occasionally damaging fences, getting into sheds and making a mess as they look for calories.“The bear’s just looking for food, doing natural behavior, but it’s creating a situation that’s not ideal,” Heeran said. “A lot of the conflict can be prevented.”Sometimes, however, that conflict can escalate, which can result in a bear being euthanized or relocated. It’s rare and wildlife officials try and prevent situations from escalating to that point, but it happens.Bear drinks from water bowlEarlier this year,the city of Monrovia erupted in furyafter a mother bear known as “Blondie” was euthanized. Officials had determined she had swiped at local residents twice, causing minor injuries. She had two cubs at the time. They are now being raised in captivity until they can hopefully be released back into the wild.Residents rallied for an alternative plan, but that effort ultimately turned into a memorial walk through the city in Blondie’s honor.“The city was not a part of that conversation or decision,” Becky Shevlin, the mayor of the city, which is peppered with monuments to black bears,toldthe Los Angeles Times in March. “We were absolutely devastated, especially when you think about her having the two little cubs.”Sherman said the spread of bear footage on social media, many of it captured by doorbell cameras that have exploded in the last decade, is a double-edged sword. On the one hand, people get to see bears being bears, doing cute things.“Bears are really cute, and a lot of the things they do are really cute … This is a real way to build meaningful empathy for wildlife, and building empathy for wildlife is a powerful motivator for conservation actions,” he said. “There is this risk of … kind of Disney-fying them. Black bears are by nature not particularly aggressive unless they are put in a dangerous or threatening situation, but they can cause damage. It’s best to give them their space.”As September draws to a close, interactions between bears and Angelenos will thin out for the season. But residents of the city will have to contend with their neighbors again come spring, alongside the mountain lions, deer and coyotes that call the city’s outskirts home.“When people move to these foothill neighborhoods, a lot of people are moving in because they think it’s a suburb of LA. But they’re not necessarily thinking they’re going to have bears in their back yard,” Sherman said. “At first it can be really scary, but the people I’ve spoken to generally become accustomed to them.”“Bears are super likable and this population of bears wouldn’t be there if people didn’t like bears so much.”Explore more on these topicsLos AngelesWildlifeCaliforniaWest CoastnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘It’s transformed the village’: the volunteers greening up Britain’s train stations | Gardens | The Guardian
description: Exclusive: Five gardening teams shortlisted for Royal Horticultural Society’s new Railway Stations in Bloom award
Author: Helena Horton
Headline: Exclusive: Five gardening teams shortlisted for Royal Horticultural Society’s new Railway Stations in Bloom award
Content: A volunteer working in the gravel garden at Alresford railway station, in Essex.Photograph: Oliver DixonView image in fullscreenA volunteer working in the gravel garden at Alresford railway station, in Essex.Photograph: Oliver DixonGardens‘It’s transformed the village’: the volunteers greening up Britain’s train stationsExclusive: Five gardening teams shortlisted for Royal Horticultural Society’s new Railway Stations in Bloom awardHelena HortonSun 20 Sep 2026 07.00 EDTLast modified on Sun 20 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleEvery year since 1964, towns across the UK have bloomed with hanging baskets and brightly coloured flowerbeds planted by residents.They wield their trowels in aid of the Royal Horticultural Society’sBritain in Bloomcompetition, a coveted accolade for the 1,600 communities that enter each year.Now, the charity is launching a new award for railway stations to honour the volunteers who keep platforms planted with cheerful flowers and pretty shrubs.Five of the best have been shortlisted for the RHS Railway Stations in Bloom competition, marked for their beauty but also for how well they welcome wildlife and withstand changing climate conditions.The winner, announced this week, was the Cardross Community Organic Garden in Scotland. The RHS said: “The judges were especially impressed by how active the group was in including different members of the community in the station’s activities, from school children, Brownies to other volunteering and gardening groups”. But all of the railway gardens are impressive.View image in fullscreenCardross community organic garden in Scotland.Photograph: RHSIt has been an extremely hot and dry summer in Alresford, Essex, but the gardeners were prepared. Working hard to cut through asphalt to create flowerbeds, they have planted a “dry garden” inspired by the horticultural pioneer Beth Chatto,who died in 2018. Also from Essex, she managed to grow plants in dry ground that had never been cultivated.“It’s transformed the centre of the village,” said the lead volunteer, Frank Belgrave. Ten years ago the station was described in the local paper as “rundown”. Now, the planting beds rival any at Chelsea flower show.View image in fullscreenThe entrance to Alresford railway station.Photograph: Oliver DixonBelgrave said residents were very pleased their station had received the spruce-up: “It’s wonderful. People sometimes stop by with plants and compost to help us, and we are very lucky to have some lovely volunteers as the garden requires constant maintenance.“We used to spend all our time watering. So we decided to seek advice and build a dry garden with drought-resistant plants.”At a windswept station on the west coast of Scotland, commuters may be surprised to find trees heaving with fruit and a thriving vegetable patch. But Jane Connolly, who heads the Cardross station volunteer group, has found a way to create such bounty.“Since March 2022, every bit of the station that can be changed, has been changed,” she said. “We do have harsh winters – we don’t take summer bedding plants as we don’t get enough out of them – we choose hardy shrubs. We put up windproofing on the shore side to protect the plants but in general we have had very few failures.”Connolly and her fellow volunteers filled the station with plants from their own gardens and visit most days to tend to them.View image in fullscreenA boat planter at Cardross station.Photograph: RHSHaving a pretty, flower-filled rail station rather than a neglected one makes a huge difference to the village, she said: “Every time we are down there, somebody will come along and peruse it and say how grateful they are with what we have done. I notice stations now wherever I go, even if it’s a window box. People come to our station just to see our gardens.”Other shortlisted stations include Maghull in Merseyside, where the ticket office’s window boxes are full of pretty flowers and volunteers have planted a woodland. At Wylde Green in Birmingham, overgrown areas were cleared and replaced with pollinator-friendly plants, creating a “bee corridor”. The volunteers carry out an annual butterfly count and have seen numbers increasing.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toDown to EarthThe planet's most important stories. Get all the week's environment news - the good, the bad and the essentialEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenPollinator-friendly plants are a focus at Wylde Green in Birmingham.Photograph: RHSKeynsham station in Somerset on a hot day looks especially exotic because volunteers have filled it with a remarkable array of succulents, of all shapes and sizes. Like the Essex gardeners, they have selected plants that will withstand hot summers.The volunteers at the stations have spoken of how social the job is and many have made friends. It also gives commuters a chance to chat. Belgrave said: “It’s very rewarding.
