But they’re not necessarily thinking they’re going to have bears in their back yard,” Sherman said. “At first it can be really scary, but the people I’ve spoken to generally become accustomed to them.”“Bears are super likable and this population of bears wouldn’t be there if people didn’t like bears so much.”Explore more on these topicsLos AngelesWildlifeCaliforniaWest CoastnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘Do you have to be dead?’: US coalminers plead for benefits as black-lung disease cases surge | US unions | The Guardian
description: Trump says he digs coal – but pneumoconiosis cases are at a 50-year high, and sick miners are mired in benefit delays
Author: Michael Sainato
Headline: Trump says he digs coal – but pneumoconiosis cases are at a 50-year high, and sick miners are mired in benefit delays
Content: A coalmine in Wharton, West Virginia. The Trump administration is moving to boost the coal industry.Photograph: Ricky Carioti for The Washington Post via Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenA coalmine in Wharton, West Virginia. The Trump administration is moving to boost the coal industry.Photograph: Ricky Carioti for The Washington Post via Getty ImagesUS unions‘Do you have to be dead?’: US coalminers plead for benefits as black-lung disease cases surgeTrump says he digs coal – but pneumoconiosis cases are at a 50-year high, and sick miners are mired in benefit delaysMichael SainatoSun 20 Sep 2026 07.00 EDTLast modified on Sun 20 Sep 2026 09.42 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFor 38 years, Josh Armes worked as a coal miner inWest Virginiaand Virginia.After retirement, Armes, 74, of Grundy, Virginia, was diagnosed with black lung disease,medically knownas coal workers’ pneumoconiosis (CWP), caused by breathing in coal dust over long periods, which irreversibly damages the lungs.Armes has required an oxygen tank to breathe for the past four years or so, along with regular doctor visits and an albuterol inhaler to help when he has trouble breathing. Even with the supplemental oxygen, he’s severely limited in what he can physically do.In 2014, Armes received notice that the federal black lung benefits he had been receiving for more than three years were being appealed against by a coal operator. For the last 12 years, he and his family have been in an appeals process limbo, trying to regain their benefits while Armes’s condition progresses.The federal black lung program wascreatedin 1969 to provide coal miners disabled by black lung with monetary compensation and medical benefits. But the Armes family is just one of many who have struggled with appeals and long delays in obtaining federal black lung benefits.Graph of black lung diseaseThose delays come as the Trump administration moves to boost the coal industry and as cases of black lung are surging – reaching a nearly 50-year high, according to data published in theAmerican Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicinelast month.According to a Mayreportby the government accountability office (GAO), 7,709 miner beneficiaries were receiving black lung benefits in 2024. The report wasrequestedin 2023 by Democratic senators Mark Warner, John Hickenlooper, Tim Kaine, and John Fetterman, who have alsointroduced legislationto improve the black-lung benefits system.In the fiscal year 2025, about 22,500 beneficiaries, including dependents, survivors, and miners, were receiving black lung benefits.Between 2013 to 2024, 40% of approved claims by the Department of Labor were disputed, generally by coal operators.The May report said miners have expressed problems with obtaining black-lung benefits. It said miners have been forced to wait several years for their claims to be approved, and raised issues with coal operators filing appeals.“I can’t figure out one thing. They sent me a paper that said I got first- and second-stage black lung. That ought to be enough, or do you have to be dead?” Armes said.View image in fullscreenLisa Emery, director of the Breathing Center and Black Lung Clinic at New River Health in Oak Hill, West Virginia, shows an X-ray of the lungs of a miner suffering from black lung disease.Photograph: Pierre Hardy/AFP/Getty ImagesHis daughter, Crystal Armes, said obtaining the black lung benefits is an arduous process, involving paying out of pocket for medical tests and finding a lawyer to take on the case. She also argued that the law should change so that coal companies shouldn’t be able to appeal after benefits are awarded.“The burden of proof lies on the coalminer to prove that he has black lung,” she said. “We have appealed it and appealed it and appealed it. Still appealing it. He [Josh] does have black lung. Hopefully, soon we will be awarded the black lung benefits again. But I’m not holding my breath on that one.”TheGAO reportsaid: “Miners in all six groups expressed their belief that mine operators were either ‘waiting for them to die’ or ‘waiting for them to give up’ so they could avoid paying benefit.” It noted between January 2013 to mid-August 2024, 390 beneficiaries whose claims were initially approved had their claims denied after appeal, leaving them responsible for paying back the benefits.According to thereport, the median length of an appealed claim was three years or more.Among 53,000 closed claims between January 2013 and August 2024, 11 claims took longer than 10 years to close. The report did not state how many open cases have surpassed 10 years.View image in fullscreenGeorge Russ, 84, a retired miner with black lung disease at a UMWA meeting in Summersville, West Virginia in August.Photograph: Robert Nickelsberg/Getty ImagesThe Armes family are still waiting for their black lungs benefits appeals process to complete, while not receiving benefits.“When you’re awarded it, they can appeal it, get a different judge, and it’s stripped away from you, which I find absolutely insane,” added Crystal Armes. “They fight you at every single step of the way. They’ll send you from one doctor to another doctor to go do another test and another test. You got to go to this doctor. You got to travel over here, and it’s very costly. And some people don’t have the means to be able to do that. I don’t feel like the process should be this difficult.”According to data published in August in theAmerican Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine, researchers at the National Institute for Safety and Occupational Health (Niosh) found 32.5% of veteran underground coalminers in central Appalachia are suffering from black lung disease, a rate unseen since 1978.Between 2020 and 2023,more than 1,700 coal minersin the US died from black lung disease.The rise in cases has beenattributedto silica dust that is more common in the coal seams being mined today.In April, E&E Greenwirereportedthat the Trump administration’s Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA) would “indefinitely delay” a federal silica dust rule, “pending judicial review” – but any judicial review is on pause due to the agency requesting an abeyance on court action.Rebecca Shelton, Director of Policy for Appalachian Citizens’ Law Center, in astatementon the agency’s freeze on enforcing the rule, said: “If the Trump administration actually cared about protecting coal miners from black lung, we’d have a strong silica rule in place right now. Instead, they are hiding behind a ridiculous legal process to delay action while miners get sick and die.”The United Mine Workers of America has pushed to unfreeze the federal silica dust rule, which would mandate engineering and ventilation controls to protect miners on the job. It was passed in April 2024, but funding for the rule wasblockedby Republicans in Congress in June 2024, and the MSHA under the Trump administrationindicated to the unionit has no plans to enforce the rule.“Every day [that] federal regulators drag their feet and sit on this rule, another working father, mother, husband, wife, sister or brother contracts an incurable, fatal disease,” Brian Sanson, president of UMWA International, in astatement. “Someone’s life is forever changed. A company’s profit margin cannot take precedence over a miner’s right to draw a breath.”Meanwhile, miners already dealing with black lung disease are still facing difficulties in trying to obtain federal benefits.“These people, like my dad, he gave his life to mining to support his family, and now you know we’ve been fighting this fight for over 10 plus years now. Everyone should be outraged by this,” added Crystal Armes. “We’re hardworking, everyday Americans who go to work every day, pay our taxes, try to do the right thing, and then, we can’t get what was promised us.”The White House deferred comment to the Department of Labor.Niosh did not respond to multiple requests for comment.A spokesperson for the MSHA at the Department of Labor said in an email: “Until pending litigation and limited rulemaking on respirable crystalline silica are resolved, MSHA continues to vigorously enforce the permissible exposure limit of 100 micrograms per cubic meter.”Explore more on these topicsUS unionsCoalMiningWest VirginiaTrump administrationUS politicsEnergyfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: NFL roundup: Bears QB Caleb Williams carted off in loss to Vikings; Saints stun Ravens  | NFL | The Guardian
description: Chicago lost quarterback Caleb Williams to a hamstring injury in their loss to Minnesota, while there was a shock result in Baltimore
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Chicago lost quarterback Caleb Williams to a hamstring injury in their loss to Minnesota, while there was a shock result in Baltimore
Content: Caleb Williams was hurt on a non-contact play.Photograph: Patrick McDermott/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenCaleb Williams was hurt on a non-contact play.Photograph: Patrick McDermott/Getty ImagesNFLNFL roundup: Bears QB Caleb Williams carted off in loss to Vikings; Saints stun RavensCaleb Williams leaves game with leg injuryTyler Shough’s late touchdown cheers New OrleansAgenciesSun 20 Sep 2026 16.34 EDTLast modified on Sun 20 Sep 2026 19.41 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMinnesota Vikings 9–3 Chicago BearsCarson Wentz passed for 143 yards, Aaron Jones Sr. rushed for 105 yards, and the visiting Minnesota Vikings (2-0) escaped ⁠with a 9-3 win over theChicago Bears, who lost their quarterback to a hamstring injury.In the fourth quarter, Williams’s injury cast a pall over the Soldier Field crowd on a gloomy, wet day along the lakefront. The Bears (1-1) trailed by three points but had first-and-goal from the Vikings’ six-yard line with less than eight minutes to go. Williams kept the ball ‌and sprinted to his left with ample green space in front of him.Suddenly, Williams stumbled and fell to his knees on a ​non-contact play. He rolled over a few times in pain until the Bears’ medical staff attended to him. He appeared to fight emotions as he was carted from the sideline ⁠to the locker room. The Bears said Williams suffered a hamstring injury.“I mean you could kind of see in real time. I’m actually happy it’s nothing with the knee,” Bears coach Ben Johnson said. “That was my first inclination. But yeah, a hamstring can be pretty damaging as well. We’ll see how bad it is tomorrow and we’ll go from there. It’s quickly you’ve got to turn the page.”Wentz completed 11 of 20 passes in ⁠his 100th career start ⁠as Minnesota (2-0) won ​despite failing to score a touchdown. Justin Jefferson had three catches for 55 yards.New Orleans Saints 24–17 Baltimore RavensTyler Shough scored on a fourth-down sneak with 1:28 remaining, and the New Orleans Saints (1-1) rallied to victory over the Baltimore Ravens (1-1). New Orleans had first down from the two before a penalty and a costly incomplete pass. On fourth-and-goal, the Saints decided against a short field goal, and Shough was ruled to have scored on a sneak. The play was upheld after a review. The Ravens, who didn’t have a first down on either of their previous two drives, made it to the New Orleans 37, but Lamar Jackson’s deep pass was intercepted by Julian Blackmon with 13 seconds left.Jacksonville Jaguars 13–20 Denver BroncosThe Denver Broncos snapped the Jacksonville Jaguars’ nine-game regular-season winning streak. Jaylen Waddle and Jonah Coleman led a big second-half comeback for the Broncos. Waddle had eight catches for 138 yards, and Coleman scored a three-yard touchdown run midway through the fourth quarter. The Broncos trailed 13-3 but responded with a field goal and a touchdown pass from Bo Nix to Nate Adkins before Coleman’s tiebreaking TD. The Jaguars had built a 13-3 lead with a touchdown run and two field goals. The Broncos tightened their defense and secured the win. Both teams are 1-1 after two games.Cincinnati Bengals 20–6 Houston TexansJoe Burrow threw two touchdown passes to Ja’Marr Chase and the Cincinnati Bengals are off to their second straight 2-0 start after notching ⁠a road victory over the Houston Texans. Burrow completed 20 of 31 passes for 207 yards and Chase had seven receptions for ⁠75 yards while posting ⁠his 14th career ​outing of two or more touchdown catches. Chase had just two catches for 12 yards in Week 1. CJ Stroud was 30-of-55 passing ⁠for 353 yards for the Texans (0-2), who lost at home for the second straight week. Dalton Schultz ​established career bests of 12 catches for 140 yards ‌for Houston, who lost ‌despite registering five sacks.Miami Dolphins 13–35 San Francisco 49ersChristian McCaffrey became the fourth-fastest player in the Super Bowl era with 100 career touchdowns, Brock Purdy played a near-perfect game and the San Francisco 49ers (2-0) overwhelmed the Miami Dolphins (0-2). The 49ers showed no signs of fatigue after beating the Los Angeles Rams in their opener in Australia and have started the season with back-to-back wins of at least 20 points for the first time in franchise history. They scored touchdowns on their first five drives of the game. Miami were dominated after spending the week by practicing in nearby Napa after losing their opener in Las Vegas.Las Vegas Raiders 26–14 Los Angeles ChargersKirk Cousins passed for 253 yards and three touchdowns while the defense forced a key turnover with less than four minutes ⁠remaining as the Las Vegas Raiders earned a victory over the Los Angeles Chargers. Tre Tucker caught five passes ⁠for 119 yards and ⁠a long ​first-half touchdown, while Cody White had two catches, both for touchdowns, as the Raiders (2-0) ended a five-game road losing streak against the Chargers and ⁠a seven-game road losing streak overall. Cousins was 19-of-29 passing with an interception while becoming the first Raiders quarterback with at least three TD passes in the ⁠first two games of a season since Ken Stabler in 1976. Justin Herbert was 15-of-27 passing for 192 ​yards with a touchdown and two interceptions ‌as the Chargers (0-2) saw a ‌four-game overall winning streak against the Raiders come to an end.Seattle Seahawks 31–7 Arizona CardinalsDrew Lock threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns to Jaxon Smith-Njigba in a stellar first start subbing for the injured Sam Darnold and the Seattle Seahawks (2-0) continued their dominance over the Arizona Cardinals (1-1). The defending Super Bowl champions have now won 10 straight over their NFC West rival dating to 2022 and closed this one by scoring the final 24 points. Smith-Njigba finished with nine catches for 155 yards and the career-high three TDs in one of the best performances of his career.Washington Commanders 20–37 Dallas CowboysDak Prescott broke Tony Romo’s franchise record for touchdown passes with four in the Dallas Cowboys’ (1-1) victory over the Washington Commanders (0-2). Prescott’s record-breaking TD toss was a 24-yarder to receiver CeeDee Lamb in the fourth quarter, the 249th of his career. It was their second TD connection of the game after Prescott had already thrown a pair to tight end Jake Ferguson. The 33-year-old Prescott has thrown 37 TDs to Lamb, the most of any target. The only major category left for Prescott to take over first place in the history of the storied franchise will be victories.Pittsburgh Steelers 3–20 New England PatriotsTreVeyon Henderson ran for a 39-yard touchdown in his season debut, Eli Ponder added a 19-yard fumble recovery for a score and the New England Patriots’ defense smothered Aaron Rodgers on the way to victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers (1-1). With the victory, Patriots coach Mike Vrabel avoided just the second 0-2 start of his eight-year coaching career. Romeo Doubs had a 63-yard catch in the third quarter to set up Andy Borregales’ second field goal of the game. Drake Maye finished 14 of 22 for 208 yards and an interception. Rodgers struggled to deal with the Patriots’ defensive pressure. The 42-year-old fumbled twice, including the one that led to Ponder’s score.Green Bay Packers 20–17 New York Jets (OT)The Green Bay Packers (1-1) overcame a 10-point fourth-quarter deficit to snap a six-game losing streak with an overtime win against the New York Jets (1-1). Trey Smack kicked a 26-yard field goal to secure the victory. Jordan Love threw two touchdown passes for the Packers, despite the team committing 14 penalties. The Jets, who also struggled with penalties, couldn’t hold their lead. Geno Smith was sacked twice in overtime, forcing the Jets to punt. Love then led a drive that set up Smack’s game-winning kick.Philadelphia Eagles 24–20 Tennessee TitansJalen Hurts threw a three-yard touchdown pass to Darius Cooper with nine seconds left, and the Philadelphia Eagles (2-0) beat the Tennessee Titans (0-2). The Eagles appeared ready to dominate Tennessee on a hot and steamy Sunday. They opened the game by stringing together three straight drives of at least 11 plays. The Titans sacked Hurts three times and picked him off twice, turning those into 10 points. The second interception set up Joey Slye’s 33-yard field goal with 1:56 left, putting Tennessee up 20-17 before Hurts, who finished with 264 yards passing and two TDs, helped his team to victory.Cleveland Browns 23–19 Tampa Bay BuccaneersDeshaun Watson earned at least a few more starts for the Cleveland Browns (1-1). Watson threw two touchdown passes, including a go-ahead 17-yard toss to Blake Whiteheart in the fourth quarter, leading the Browns to a comeback victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-2) in a game that was delayed two hours, 12 minutes because of lightning. The Buccaneers were driving and had a second-and-4 at the Cleveland 28 when the game was suspended at the two-minute warning. When the game finally resumed, heavy rain started falling again, and the Bucs could not pull off the win.Carolina Panthers 34–3 Atlanta FalconsBryce Young threw for 287 yards and three touchdowns, including two to Darren Waller, Carolina’s Devin Lloyd returned one of his two interceptions for a touchdown and the Panthers (1-1) crushed the short-handed Atlanta Falcons (0-2). The Panthers took their fourth straight win in the NFC South rivalry. Young completed 23 of 36 passes as he improved to 5-1 against the Falcons. He set a franchise record with 448 yards passing in a 30-27 overtime win to cap last season’s sweep. With Cooper Rush at quarterback, the Falcons had more offensive woes. Rookie Jack Strand replaced Rush late in the game.Explore more on these topicsNFLUS sportsChicago BearsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Manchester United’s engine room runs out of steam as fans voice frustration | Manchester United | The Guardian
description: Michael Carrick’s side were short on inspiration, despite the summer spend in midfield, and the lack of quality in the final third was stark
Author: Jacob Steinberg
Headline: Michael Carrick’s side were short on inspiration, despite the summer spend in midfield, and the lack of quality in the final third was stark
Content: Youri Tielemans on the ball against Fulham but he has yet to show the form that made him so influential for Aston Villa.Photograph: John Patrick Fletcher/Action Plus/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenYouri Tielemans on the ball against Fulham but he has yet to show the form that made him so influential for Aston Villa.Photograph: John Patrick Fletcher/Action Plus/ShutterstockManchester UnitedAnalysisManchester United’s engine room runs out of steam as fans voice frustrationJacob Steinbergat Craven CottageCarrick’s side were short on inspiration, despite the summer spend in midfield, and the lack of quality in the final third was starkSun 20 Sep 2026 15.14 EDTLast modified on Sun 20 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTShareOne of the more damning aspects of Manchester United’s tortured rebuild is their inability to multitask. So much money has been frittered away, pushing United into the ridiculous position of going one position at a time each summer. Last year was all about the attack and the recent window was about central midfield, even though the options at full-back do not look strong enough to cope with a season back in the Champions League.United remain a listless, drifting operation. The ownership is reviled and the fanbase is becoming increasingly mutinous. It was not just Gary Neville seeing red as he commentated on United’s dismal efforts away to winless Fulham. There was an ominous shift in the mood in the away end at Craven Cottage, summed up by the boos that greetedMichael Carricksubstituting Kobbie Mainoo with 10 minutes to go.Cunha strikes late to deny Fulham and salvage point for Manchester UnitedRead moreCarrick filled in as an emergency centre-back when United last lost this fixture, way back in December 2009. This has been a happy hunting ground since then and there was a sense of inevitability to United saving themselves on Sunday, although that was more to do with Fulham’s nerves at 1-0 up than any great show of defiance from the visitors when a third defeat in the space of a week was on the cards.The late equaliser was fortunate, Matheus Cunha’s potshot hitting the luckless David Affengruber before going in. Bernd Leno was deceived in the Fulham goal but United did not fool anyone by stirring only after falling behind to Lisandro Martínez’s slapstick own goal. Speaking on Sky Sports, Neville called out the lack of effort during the 15 minutes before Fulham’s goal. Players went through the motions and pulled out of tackles, while the manner of the concession was feeble.United could not get out of their box and when Cunha melted in a challenge with Calvin Bassey, the Fulham centre-back barrelled forward before testing Senne Lammens, only for Martínez to turn the rebound past his goalkeeper. It was a farcical goal and in keeping with the flow at that stage. United had no control or presence in midfield. Bruno Fernandes was the No 10 and Mainoo was deeper with Youri Tielemans, signed from Aston Villa last summer, but the ease with which Sander Berge and Shea Charles dominated for Fulham was proof that Carrick’s renovation in the engine room remains a work in progress.It is interesting that United targeted quantity during a summer in which rival clubs were spending so much on midfielders. Andrey Santos, an unused substitute here, joined from Chelsea for £50m but is yet to prove himself in English football. Tielemans was an opportunistic £35m. Manchester City spent £300m on three midfielders, while Arsenal added depth by buying Bruno Guimarães for £75m. Carrick will hope that Carlos Baleba, back from an ankle injury, makes his debut after the international break.United were outrun by Fulham. They looked unfit and need Baleba to provide oomph. There were times when Fulham ripped through the middle, particularly in transition. Alex Iwobi surged away from Tielemans during the first half. Josh King’s raids down the inside-right channel caught the eye and Fulham repeatedly cut through before half-time, only for poor finishing to let them down.Carrick raised eyebrows by saying United controlled a lot of the first half. Cunha was close to the mark by saying Fulham “put in more energy than us” at the start of the second half. One worry is that the players are already not following Carrick’s instructions. Another is that the window-by-window rebuild has still left United short of ideas in midfield and attack.View image in fullscreenBruno Fernandes was unable to inspire his teammates to beat Fulham.Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/ReutersThose areas were meant to have been sorted. Instead, United were ponderous on and off the ball. There were flashes in attack but they did not convince. While allowances have to be made for Benjamin Sesko missing out through injury, leaving United short of an effective target man to introduce, the lack of quality in the final third was stark.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionMichael Carrick disputes Manchester United’s lack of fitness after draw at FulhamRead moreOnly a defensive error from Fulham led to Fernandes hitting the post at 0-0. Cunha also clipped the woodwork, albeit via a heavy deflection, and Marcus Rashford wasted two opportunities.It is odd that the new-look attack still means a start for Rashford, who was up for sale last year. He played on the left and flattered to deceive before being taken off. Yet Rashford is not the only United forward who can look promising before drifting out of games. Bryan Mbeumo almost equalised but had an inconsistent game on the right. Cunha looks uncomfortable playing as the No 9 but Carrick does not appear to trust Sesko.Carrick is under pressure. United have five points from five games and are already out of the Carabao Cup. The doubts over whether Carrick deserved the job will grow. But he is not the first United manager to struggle because of wider failings and is unlikely to be the last. It was not ideal, after all, that Carrick had to bring Joshua Zirkzee on when United were chasing an equaliser. The Dutch forward has five league goals since joining two years ago. Why has he not been sold? Some rebuild.Explore more on these topicsManchester UnitedFulhamMichael CarrickanalysisShareReuse this content

title: ‘A terrible, terrible accident’: Cubs’ Bregman undergoing CT scans after taking foul ball to face | Chicago Cubs | The Guardian
description: Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman was taken to the hospital for tests after being struck in the face by a foul ball
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman was taken to the hospital for tests after being struck in the face by a foul ball
Content: Alex Bregman was escorted off the field after being struck by the ball.Photograph: Kareem Elgazzar/APView image in fullscreenAlex Bregman was escorted off the field after being struck by the ball.Photograph: Kareem Elgazzar/APChicago Cubs‘A terrible, terrible accident’: Cubs’ Bregman undergoing CT scans after taking foul ball to faceThird baseman was standing near on-deck circlePlayer taken to hospital for X-rays and CT scanAssociated PressSun 20 Sep 2026 18.20 EDTLast modified on Sun 20 Sep 2026 18.21 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleChicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman was taken to the hospital for tests after being struck in the face by a foul ball while standing in front of the on-deck circle during Sunday’s game against the Cincinnati Reds.There was no immediate decision on whether Bregman, who was taken for X-rays and CT scans, would travel with the team back to Chicago after the Cubs’ 9-1 win.“He got hit in the left cheekbone essentially, under the eye,” Cubs manager Craig Counsell said. “I don’t know anything more than that right now. He was bleeding from his nose a little. There’s some swelling. It’s a terrible, terrible accident. We hope he’s OK.”Allow content provided by a third party?This article includes content hosted onembed.bsky.app. We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as the provider may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content,click 'Allow and continue'.Allow and continueIn the fourth inning, Michael Busch checked his swing and fouled off a pitch from Reds Luis Mey that struck Bregman, who immediately jogged toward the Cubs’ dugout with his hand covering the left side of his face.Bregman was escorted by a trainer down the dugout steps and into the clubhouse, with blood visible on his face.“It just happens so fast,” Busch said. “[Mey] is throwing the ball hard and it comes off hard. Any time it enters the head area, it’s always a scary thing. We try to focus on the game, but it’s tough. Hopefully he’s OK, first and foremost.”Bregman is batting .262 with 26 home runs and 89 RBIs after signing a $175m, five-year free-agent deal in January.“You just hope your friend is OK,” Cubs outfielder Pete Crow-Armstrong said. “That’s the news that I’m hoping for. But scary stuff. Such a rarity.”Counsell said he hasn’t thought about how a potential long-term absence for Bregman could affect his postseason roster plans.“You know, we’ve got to get good results from the hospital,” Counsell said. “He got hit in the face [so] you’re worried just about his general wellbeing first. I want to get a good report first.”Explore more on these topicsChicago CubsMLBBaseballUS sportsShareReuse this content

title: Lynx’s Olivia Miles breaks Caitlin Clark’s WNBA rookie scoring record | Minnesota Lynx | The Guardian
description: Olivia Miles broke Caitlin Clark’s WNBA rookie scoring record on Sunday in the Minnesota Lynx’s 101-89 victory over the Connecticut Sun
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Olivia Miles broke Caitlin Clark’s WNBA rookie scoring record on Sunday in the Minnesota Lynx’s 101-89 victory over the Connecticut Sun
Content: Olivia Miles is having a superb first season in the WNBA.Photograph: Abbie Parr/APView image in fullscreenOlivia Miles is having a superb first season in the WNBA.Photograph: Abbie Parr/APMinnesota LynxLynx’s Olivia Miles breaks Caitlin Clark’s WNBA rookie scoring recordGuard was named an All-Star in first WNBA seasonMiles has broken several records in first campaignAssociated PressSun 20 Sep 2026 18.09 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleOlivia Milesbroke Caitlin Clark’s WNBA rookie scoring record on Sunday in the Minnesota Lynx’s 101-89 victory over the Connecticut Sun.Miles, who finished with 21 points, was tied with Clark at 769 points coming into the game and moved to the top of the list when she made a free throw in the second quarter. The Lynx rookie came into the game averaging 19.7 points, 6.0 assists and 4.7 rebounds, and is a big reason theteam have the best record in the WNBA.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Weekly for the 2026 WNBA seasonSign up toWNBA 30A limited run women’s basketball newsletter dedicated to the league’s historic 30th season.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionOlivia Miles: the goggled wonder woman pulverizing WNBA opponents in her rookie seasonRead more“It’s special, but it means we’re more so working well as a team. I have great teammates around me, great vets who allow me to be me out there,” Miles said. “It wouldn’t be possible without one, a coach that believes in you and then two, having teammates that have my back. So it’s really special to obviously be able to accomplish that with such a great team and on a win as well.”Miles was 7 of 10 from the field and made all six of her free-throw attempts. The All-Star guard, who was selected second in the draft after playing college ball at Notre Dame and TCU, got off to a slow start against the Sun, going scoreless in the first quarter. Her record-breaking free throw came 29 seconds into the second quarter.Miles and Clark accomplished their feats in 40 games.The Lynx star already had broken a couple of rookie records held by Clark. She hit eight three-pointers in a win over Golden State on 4 June to set the league record for most by a rookie in a game. That was one more than Clark’s best. Miles also became the fastest rookie to reach 350 points, 100 rebounds and 100 assists in her career, doing it in 21 games – one quicker than Clark and former Charlotte Sting guard Andrea Stinson.Explore more on these topicsMinnesota LynxCaitlin ClarkWNBABasketballUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Evenepoel wins fourth world time trial title in a row, Reusser retains her crown | Cycling | The Guardian
description: Belgium’s Remco Evenepoel won the men’s time trial title for the fourth time in a row, while the Swiss rider Marlen Reusser defended her women’s crown
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Belgium’s Remco Evenepoel won the men’s time trial title for the fourth time in a row, while the Swiss rider Marlen Reusser defended her women’s crown
Content: Remco Evenepoel celebrates his fourth successive world time trial title after dominating in Montreal.Photograph: Jasper Jacobs/Belga/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenRemco Evenepoel celebrates his fourth successive world time trial title after dominating in Montreal.Photograph: Jasper Jacobs/Belga/ShutterstockCyclingEvenepoel wins fourth world time trial title in a row, Reusser retains her crownRemco Evenepoel dominates men’s event in MontrealMarlen Reusser denies Zoe Backstedt in women’s raceAgence France-PresseSun 20 Sep 2026 16.28 EDTFirst published on Sun 20 Sep 2026 13.16 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRemco Evenepoel etched his name into the history books with a dominant fourth successive men’s world time-trial victory in Montreal on Sunday.The 2024 Olympic champion came into the race as the overwhelming favourite and he did not disappoint. Evenepoel was already more than 30 seconds ahead of the rest by the second intermediate time check, just over halfway along the 39.2km (24.4 mile) route.Sports quiz of the week: records, hazards, complaints and boring eventsRead moreBy the time he reached the finish line, the 26-year-old Belgian had put almost a minute into second-placed Filippo Ganna of Italy, with the French rider Paul Seixas taking third another 15 seconds back. Evenepoel has not lost a time trial since the 2025 Tour de France.Evenepoel becomes the first man to win the time trial world title four times in a row, while also equalling the record number of overall titles held by Germany’s Tony Martin and the Swiss rider Fabian Cancellara.He has enjoyed his best season to date so far this year, winning the Amstel Gold Race, Clásica San Sebastián and Grand Prix de Québec, as well as finishing second behind Tadej Pogacar this year at the Tour de France.Ganna started slowly and was only 10th at the first time check, but by the third he had moved up into second spot. But he could not make any headway into Evenepoel, who did not stop increasing his lead from the start to the finish.The young Swedish rider Jakob Soderqvist, the under-23 champion in this discipline last year, was second to Evenepoel at the first two time checks but faded over the last 10km and finished fifth. The teenager Seixas gauged his effort better and put in a strong ride over the final 10km to finish third.Earlier on Sunday, Marlen Reusser retained her world time-trial title as her expected main challenger, Demi Vollering, finished a disappointing eighth.Reusser secured an ultimately comfortable victory in Montreal, winning her second world championship after triumphing last year in Kigali – but not before the young British rider Zoe Backstedt gave her a scare.Backstedt had been quickest at the first two intermediate time checks on the course but Reusser powered away in the second half of the race to beat the 21-year-old by 40sec. Germany’s Franziska Koch finished third, a further 6sec back.View image in fullscreenMarlen Reusser (centre) receives her gold medal with Zoe Backstedt (left) winning silver and Franziska Koch (right) bronze.Photograph: Chris Auld/SWpix.com/Shutterstock“It’s a good present,” said Reusser, who was competing on her 35th birthday. “I also thought, win or not, I have something to celebrate.“From the side of pacing and understanding how fast you should go and how you should also cope with these challenges on the way, I was really nervous. I was not really sure, because we don’t have time trials like this often … I’m used to doing 20km.”Reusser has been virtually unbeatable in races against the clock in the past few years. The Swiss cyclist is a four-time European champion and has won time-trial stages at the Tour de France Femmes and Giro d’Italia Women.Backstedt had been a junior and twice under-23 world champion in the discipline, but this race was around 12km further than any previous time trial in which she had competed. Koch’s bronze medal continued a dream season for the German, who won Paris-Roubaix in April. Vollering, the European road race champion, was never in the running for a medal.Elsewhere,Mathieu van der Poelwarmed up for his bid for a second world road rice title with a long-range solo break on the final stage of the Tour of Luxembourg .The Dutch star broke clear just over a couple of kilometres into the 177km stage and held on in front all day to win by more than a minute. Van der Poel’s run is thought to be one of the longest solo breaks in the history of cycling.The 2023 world road race champion will be one of the favourites in Montreal next weekend, where the reigning champion Pogacar will be missing because of injury.“That was not the plan before the start, but I found myself alone from the start of the race in fact, and I just rode my tempo the whole day,” Van der Poel said. Italy’s Davide Piganzoli finished fourth on the stage to secure overall victory.Explore more on these topicsCyclingUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Elvira’s fairytale crumbles at the last to hand Spaun PGA Championship title | European Tour | The Guardian
description: Manuel Elvira endured a nightmare final hole at Wentworth to see victory at the PGA Championship slip through his fingers and hand the trophy to JJ Spain
Author: Ewan Murray
Headline: Manuel Elvira endured a nightmare final hole at Wentworth to see victory at the PGA Championship slip through his fingers and hand the trophy to JJ Spain
Content: Manuel Elvira is unable to hide his disappointment as he lets victory slip away on the final hole.Photograph: Colorsport/Daniel Bearham/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenManuel Elvira is unable to hide his disappointment as he lets victory slip away on the final hole.Photograph: Colorsport/Daniel Bearham/ShutterstockEuropean TourElvira’s fairytale crumbles at the last to hand Spaun PGA Championship titleWorld No 294 lets victory slip in agonising fashionJJ Spaun triumphs by two shots at WentworthEwan Murrayat WentworthSun 20 Sep 2026 14.29 EDTLast modified on Sun 20 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleWe will come to JJ Spaun and Jeremy Clarkson later. Only those without an ounce of compassion in their body could feel no sympathy for Manuel Elvira. The Spaniard, without a professional win to his name, stood on the 18th fairway at Wentworth’s West Course with one of golf’s most extraordinary stories in his grasp. Having just eagled the 71st hole and found the short grass on the friendly par five, the 30-year-old who began tournament week as the world’s 294th ranked player knew a birdie would seal the PGA Championship title. A par would force Spaun into a playoff.What happened next was a form of sporting torture rather than the realisation of a fairytale. Elvira pulled his layup into a bunker, flew the green, fluffed a chip into another sand trap and missed a bogey putt from 4ft. He did exceptionally well not to burst into tears. The disastrous 18th meant Elvira finished in a four-way tie for second place. Even Spaun, a winner on his Wentworth debut, had to be bashful at the manner of success.Jon Rahm shoots 78-77 and slumps off in last place at PGA ChampionshipRead more“It is devastating that I hit the wrong shot on the layup and left myself the toughest shot in the fairway bunker,” Elvira said. “I wasn’t able to pull it off. I have played some of the best golf probably of my life.”Beware the jilted golfer. Spaun arrived in England carrying a grudge at being overlooked for next weekend’s Presidents Cup where the US will take on an international team at Medinah. His omission was odd even before this victory.Rory McIlroy, during post-tournament media duties, had assumed Spaun was part of Brandt Snedeker’s team. Americans have now won three of the last six editions of the DP World Tour’s flagship event.“I played with a huge chip on my shoulder,” said Spaun. “I definitely had something to prove this week but everything happens for a reason.” Spaun was already a major champion. This win means it is seriously difficult to believe Spaun will be ignored again when the US take on Europe in Ireland at next year’s Ryder Cup. His game can travel.View image in fullscreenJJ Spaun lifts the trophy on his Wentworth debut.Photograph: Colorsport/Daniel Bearham/ShutterstockSpaun and his family have become regular visitors to the Cotswolds after developing a fondness for the television show Clarkson’s Farm. To add to a wacky closing scene in Surrey, Spaun’s wife was waving a Clarkson mask around as the champion was confirmed. “I’ve kind of blossomed into this player I never thought I could be,” Spaun said. “To take my game across the world – more specifically here in England, a place that’s dear to my family’s heart – the stars kind of aligned for me to come out on top.”Spaun’s fourth round of 67 included four birdies in the final five holes. Seventeen under par proved sufficient to take the trophy by two strokes. Those alongside Elvira were McIlroy, Aaron Rai and Adam Scott.McIlroy’s weekend involved missed opportunity. One realises how special a talent the Masters champion is when reaching 15 under par despite missing chance upon chance. McIlroy’s 68 included four birdie misses from 10ft or closer. His irritation at what might have been can be partly offset by the making up of decent ground on Patrick Reed in the DP World Tour’s order of merit race. Reed versus McIlroy promises to be quite the spectacle between now and mid November.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toSport in FocusOur picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown inEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“I feel like my game is heading in the right direction,” said McIlroy, who is in the midst of technical changes. “When I look at my swing on video, I still don’t like what I am seeing. It is going to take time.Golfisn’t just about the swing, you also have to chip and putt. My swing is not where I want it to be.” Still, McIlroy produced the shot of the day with an iron from trees at the 12th which hooked 80 yards before resting just short of the green.Joost Luiten, Matt Fitzpatrick, Ryan Fox and Filippo Celli completed the top nine. This was, however, a story dominated by one man. And not, given the circumstances, the one who came out on top.Explore more on these topicsEuropean TourRory McIlroyGolfnewsShareReuse this content

title: Carrick disputes Cunha’s claim that Manchester United lacked energy in Fulham draw | Manchester United | The Guardian
description: Michael Carrick has said his Manchester United side ‘kept pushing’ and rejected Matheus Cunha’s claim that Fulham ‘put in more energy’
Author: David Hytner
Headline: Michael Carrick has said his Manchester United side ‘kept pushing’ and rejected Matheus Cunha’s claim that Fulham ‘put in more energy’
Content: Michael Carrick said he is ‘not despondent and down because we’re showing some good signs’.Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenMichael Carrick said he is ‘not despondent and down because we’re showing some good signs’.Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/ReutersManchester UnitedCarrick disputes Cunha’s claim that Manchester United lacked energy in Fulham drawMichael Carrick insists team ‘kept pushing’ for levellerMatheus Cunha: ‘Fulham put in more energy than us’David Hytnerat Craven CottageSun 20 Sep 2026 15.49 EDTLast modified on Sun 20 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMichael Carrick rejected the suggestion that hisManchester Unitedplayers lacked physical fitness after they snatched a last-gasp 1-1 draw at Fulham on Sunday. The statistics showed the home side ran a collective 6.6km more than United, whose goalscorer in the 89th minute – Matheus Cunha – was critical of his team’s efforts.United were poor after the restart at 0-0, leading up to a disastrous Lisandro Martínez own goal in the 63rd minute, with Cunha saying they had to give more. “In the beginning of the second half,Fulhamput in more energy than us and we cannot accept this,” Cunha said.Manchester United’s engine room runs out of puff as fans begin to voice frustration | Jacob SteinbergRead moreThe draw was not the result Carrick or United wanted after a week during which they lost the derby against Manchester City and exited the Carabao Cup against Brighton; both matches were at Old Trafford. Carrick will take it under the circum­stances and he tried to ­highlight the positives which he said took in the never-say-die spirit of his ­players. They fought until the end and were rewarded when ­Cunha’s shot from distance took a heavy deflection off the ­Fulham defender David ­Affengruber to wrongfoot Bernd Leno.Carrick said he did not agree with Cunha’s comment about the collective energy levels. “I don’t, ­particularly,” the manager said. “The way we finished the game … it didn’t look like that for me. I was quite happy with the way we finished the game. We kept pushing. I don’t think that’s an issue, no.“The response [to the own goal] was really pleasing … the way we went about trying to get back into the game. [We] kept the ideas, kept the patience, kept the real purpose to it. We finished on a positive, which is a small step for us … without ­getting carried away it’s a good step. We came to take three points but at least we’ve taken something to build on ­moving forward.“It has been pretty fine ­margins [so far this season] that have flipped it [the wrong way]. I know we can do better, we need to do better at certain things. But I’m not despondent and down because we’re showing some good signs.”A section of the United support booed Carrick’s decision to ­withdraw Kobbie Mainoo in the 80th minute; the manager sent on Mason Mount in his place. “There’s always going to be ­certain reactions when you’re ­making changes,” Carrick said. “I ­understand. We’re chasing the game and ­everyone’s a little bit emotional. I don’t take any negatives or offence to it.”Carrick was asked whether he felt a certain deflation among the fans, who have been expecting a big season from United. “It’s still a big season ahead,” he said. “It’s a long season and you’re going to have spells through it. That’s part of the journey.“I’m not playing it down. We wanted more points. I’m not saying everything’s great. I understand the frustration. But deflation is certainly not what we have within the club. The players didn’t have that on the pitch today and that’s what will carry us through the season.”The Fulham manager, Álvaro Arbeloa, was unhappy with the officials and he claimed they did not want United to lose after what had ­happened in the City game last ­Sunday when Erling Haaland’s ­winner was allowed to stand despite his teammate, Enzo Fernández, being in an offside position.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionQuick GuideNeville says United 'absolutely pathetic'ShowGary Neville branded Manchester United’s early second-half display against Fulham as the worst he had seen in more than 45 years. Reflecting on United’s lethargic, error-strewn start to the half, the Sky co-commentator called the period “absolutely pathetic”, saying: “I’ve watched Manchester United since the age of five and that’s the worst 15 minutes I’ve ever seen. I’ve never seen such a lack of effort. What must Michael Carrick be thinking?”Guardian sportWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Arbeloa highlighted what he said was a soft free-kick in Harry ­Maguire’s favour on halfway, which came 35 seconds before Cunha’s equaliser. Maguire felt the contact from the ­Fulham substitute, César Palacios.“All the fouls for them,” Arbeloa said to Sky Sports straight after the game. “You can see before they scored, the foul against Maguire … he’s a guy who is 100 kilos. Every decision was for them. And I knew. I knew after the game against Manchester City that they [would not] let Manchester United lose here.”Arbeloa rowed back on his comments in his main press conference but still said he was “not really happy”. The referee, Peter Bankes, gave Fulham the benefit of the doubt in the 86th minute when a Martínez shot hit Calvin Bassey’s hand inside the area. Bassey did put his hand up but it remained close to his body.Explore more on these topicsManchester UnitedMichael CarrickFulhamnewsShareReuse this content

title: Maresca dismisses title talk as ‘too early’ after Manchester City take over at the top | Manchester City | The Guardian
description: The manager said after the frantic home victory against Sunderland: ‘I prefer to win 1-0 than 5-3 but I expected a very difficult game’
Author: Jamie Jackson
Headline: The manager said after the frantic home victory against Sunderland: ‘I prefer to win 1-0 than 5-3 but I expected a very difficult game’
Content: Enzo Maresca said Manchester City ‘need to avoid conceding goals’ like the three they did against Sunderland.Photograph: Roger Evans/Action Plus/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenEnzo Maresca said Manchester City ‘need to avoid conceding goals’ like the three they did against Sunderland.Photograph: Roger Evans/Action Plus/ShutterstockManchester CityMaresca dismisses title talk as ‘too early’ after Manchester City take over at the top‘I prefer to win 1-0 than 5-3 but expected a difficult game’Semenyo scored twice in 5-3 victory against SunderlandJamie Jacksonat the Etihad StadiumSun 20 Sep 2026 13.22 EDTLast modified on Sun 20 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleEnzo Maresca dismissed ­Manchester City pulling ahead in the title race afterSunday’s 5-3 win over Sunderland, with the manager stating it is “too early” in the season.The frantic victory at the Etihad Stadium gave City 15 points from their opening five league matches, three more than Arsenal after the championslost at Brightonon Saturday. Maresca was asked about his team being top before the three-week international break.Semenyo helps chaotic Manchester City beat Sunderland despite Brobbey hat-trickRead more“It’s much better to win games,” he said. “In this moment, it’s better to have three points more than less, no doubt. But at the same time, we know that it’s quite early. The international break is good. We can review what we have done and what we can do better, and at the same time, we can relax a little more.”Of the victory againstSunderland, Maresca said: “I prefer to win 1-0 than 5-3 but I expected a very difficult game – I knew how good they are, off the ball, very aggressive. I knew it was a difficult game but happy because we found a way to win the game.“We scored five. We could have scored probably more goals. So that means that we create enough, but at the same time we need to avoid conceding goals like today. We had four clean sheets in a row and today we conceded three goals.”City twice took the lead in the first half after goals from Enzo Fernández and Rayan Cherki, yet each time Sunderland found equalisers from Brian Brobbey, before Antoine Semenyo’s 43rd-minute strike gave the home team a 3-2 half-time lead.After the break the winger’s second made it 4-2 before Brobbey completed his hat-trick to make it 4-3 on 59 minutes. While Erling Haaland’s late strike completed the scoring Brobbey became the first player to score three and be on the losing side in the Premier League since Roque Santa Cruz in Blackburn’s 5-3 loss at Wigan in December 2007.At 3-2 Elliot Anderson appeared to handle in his area but was not penalised and City subsequently launched the attack that created Semenyo’s second.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionRégis Le Bris, Sunderland’s manager, said: “It was hard to see that as not a handball. It is what it is and we have to accept the decision. It’s hard to comment. It’s a defeat, but we are proud of the level of the squad. It is really tight at this level against one of the best teams in Europe. A half chance gets punished, and it’s probably the lesson of the day.”Explore more on these topicsManchester CityEnzo MarescaSunderlandnewsShareReuse this content

title: Isak pounces to give Liverpool victory on Iraola’s return to Bournemouth | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Alexander Isak slotted home from close range after a Cody Gakpo cross in the 57th minute to give Liverpool a welcome win 1-0 at Bournemouth
Author: Ben Fisher
Headline: Alexander Isak slotted home from close range after a Cody Gakpo cross in the 57th minute to give Liverpool a welcome win 1-0 at Bournemouth
Content: Alexander Isak gives the Liverpool fans the thumbs-up after scoring a second-half winner.Photograph: Paul Childs/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenAlexander Isak gives the Liverpool fans the thumbs-up after scoring a second-half winner.Photograph: Paul Childs/Action Images/ReutersPremier LeagueIsak pounces to give Liverpool victory on Iraola’s return to BournemouthBen Fisherat the Vitality StadiumSun 20 Sep 2026 11.06 EDTLast modified on Sun 20 Sep 2026 18.08 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAt the final whistle, victory secured, Andoni Iraola embraced both his current players and those he guided to new heights atBournemouthlast season. Liverpool are not yet the overwhelming, suffocating force Iraola wants them to become but they did enough to claim three points here, Alexander Isak capping a peculiar performance with a simple finish.Cody Gakpo was again the architect, the Dutchman the supplier for all four of Isak’s goals this season. Isak’s only other shot before scoring was to balloon a first-time effort high and wide but his second-half strike was sufficient to return Liverpool to winning ways in thePremier League.Semenyo helps perfect Manchester City beat Sunderland 5-3 after Brobbey hat-trickRead morePerhaps it was inevitable that these teams would neutralise each other. On Iraola’s final day at Bournemouth’s training base he spent an hour in the company of his successor, Marco Rose, who is yet to taste victory in the Premier League. The pair stopped talking only because Tiago Pinto, Bournemouth’s sporting director, interrupted to remind them there were other things on the agenda.“We knew what we were going to get, they knew what they were going to get and maybe you could see it,” Rose said. “It is mostly the same after our games; I sit here after a good performance, but you don’t get points for good performances. You have to force wins.”Amine Adli, sidelined because of a calf injury, scored a95th-minute winnerin a 3-2 victory for Bournemouth in this fixture last season but there was no such chaos to this game. The only clear sight of goal arrived approaching the hour when Gakpo bypassed Adrien Truffert down the right flank and squared, the ball trickling towards Isak on the edge of the six-yard box.A few minutes earlier Isak had sent Iraola retreating to the away dugout. “Yes, yes,” Iraola said, encouraging Isak as the Sweden striker made tracks on the wing, white shirts attacking the box, only for his wayward cross to end up with the ball flying towards the scaffolding structure in a corner of this ground, part of Bournemouth’s ongoing stadium upgrade.View image in fullscreenAndoni Iraola applauds the fans after victory at the Vitality Stadium.Photograph: Ian Walton/APIn midweek, Iraola was rooting for his former club on their European bow but promised a businesslike return to Bournemouth and stepped off one of the twoLiverpoolteam coaches with a game face. Tommy Elphick, who captained Bournemouth to the Premier League in 2015 and followed Iraola to Liverpool, embraced old colleagues pitchside before the warm-up.“I love it because I love this club and it is growing,” Iraola said after Liverpool extended their unbeaten start to seven games in all competitions. “They will enjoy European nights here. This stadium will become a lot nicer. I was delighted to see a lot of the people I appreciate so much.”All the niceties, Iraola said, could wait until afterwards. Pablo de la Torre, his fitness coach who was part of his Bournemouth staff, made that clear within the opening 30 seconds, wresting the ball away from Adam Smith to delay the hosts taking a quick throw‑in. Bournemouth were intent on building ontheir history‑making winon Thursday in the Basque Country and had the best chance of the first half, Alisson’s smart right-hand save preventing Evanilson’s front-post flick squeezing in at his near post.Dominik Szoboszlai dropped a typically vicious free-kick wide of Djordje Petrovic’s post and Petrovic saved a deflected Bradley Barcola shot, but Liverpool spent much of the first half containing Bournemouth’s threats. Iraola conceded that his side were slow out of the blocks.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“We didn’t start with the intensity that is required to win here,” he said. “You never play comfortably here – Bournemouth put you under pressure and you have to adapt.”Liverpool only teased glimpses of quality. Florian Wirtz saw a disguised pass for Isak cut out and Bournemouth flew forward, the alert and again impressive Jérémy Jacquet extinguishing the danger as Ryan Christie flung his body to connect with a low cross. Christie chopped inside Szoboszlai close to the touchline and Scott switched play with a pinged diagonal pass.Bournemouth seemed to be growing in confidence but then Gakpo breezed past Truffert, usually such a dependable performer who last week was given a France recall. Gakpo crossed from the right and while James Hill dived in to stop the threat of Wirtz at the front post, the ball dropped to an unmarked Isak on the edge of the six‑yard box to stroke the ball in.It was not a nerveless finale. Iraola hopped on the touchline as Scott, poised to make his England debut in this international window, lined up a 90th-minute free‑kick. After Liverpool won a free-kick deep into four minutes of stoppage time, Iraola crossed his hands and frantically pointed his players towards the scoreboard showing there were only a matter of seconds remaining. Moments later, it was a case of job done. “I think in life you always get what you deserve,” a phlegmatic Rose said. “One error is too much, that’s the point.”Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueBournemouthLiverpoolmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Jonathan David earns Atlético precious win over 10-man Real Madrid in fractious derby | La Liga | The Guardian
description: Atlético Madrid took a 2-0 lead against Real Madrid, who had Dean Huijsen sent off, and survived after Antonio Rüdiger’s late goal, to win 2-1
Author: Sid Lowe
Headline: Atlético Madrid took a 2-0 lead against Real Madrid, who had Dean Huijsen sent off, and survived after Antonio Rüdiger’s late goal, to win 2-1
Content: Jonathan David (left) high-fives Giuliano Simeone after scoring Atlético Madrid’s second goal.Photograph: Juan Barbosa/ReutersView image in fullscreenJonathan David (left) high-fives Giuliano Simeone after scoring Atlético Madrid’s second goal.Photograph: Juan Barbosa/ReutersLa LigaJonathan David earns Atlético precious win over 10-man Real Madrid in fractious derbySid Loweat the Riyadh Air MetropolitanoSun 20 Sep 2026 14.10 EDTLast modified on Sun 20 Sep 2026 19.19 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleOn the eve of the derby, Diego Simeone described this as a special week in Madrid, a “tremendous energy about the city”, and it closed the way he wanted. He had enjoyed the Formula One, he said, and he had enjoyed seeing Shakira in concert, but he enjoyed this even more. At least he did by the time the last of many, many blows on the referee’s whistle brought it to an end, sprinting up the tunnel punching the air. Having been 2-0 up against 10 men through goals from Álex Grimaldo and Jonathan David, seemingly in control, a late header from Antonio Rüdiger awoke old ghosts and brought tension, but they did it.José Mourinho’s first derby back atReal Madridended in defeat and recriminations: he turned up in the press conference with a picture of two moments in which he claimed that Lee Kang-in and Cristian Romero should have been sent off and insisted the story was there. And yet there are other questions: over the way Dean Huijsen gave away the penalty and got the red card that tilted the game against them, and how his team played, how little they did.Carlos Espí gives Real Madrid hope in the face of Barcelona’s La Liga storm | Sid LoweRead moreIt is 13 years since these two managers met in this fixture, their last time the night Atlético won the Cup at the Santiago Bernabéu. Then, Mourinho was sent off and didn’t collect his medal from the king. His return has been driven by nostalgia and it was like old times in the press room. He and Simeone are “companions of war”, he had said, and so it was.It was not until the 39th minute that there was a shot on target when Atlético’s Jan Oblak pushed Arda Guler’s long-range effort away. Otherwise, there was little football but it had been heating up from the beginning, Guler the first to confront the referee after a foul by Álex Baena. To which he responded by fouling Baena back. From the bench, something was said and Diego Simeone was booked; the scene had been set.Atlético probed from wide, almost always the right wing. An advance on that side led to Ibrahima Konaté doubting and Giuliano Simeone flashing wide. At the other end Vinícius Júnior shot over twice before the half’s most significant moment. Which, appropriately, was not about the play.Jude Bellingham slid in to tackle Romero and the referee showed him a yellow. Bellingham, his teammates and the bench were incensed and the video assistant referee was engaged. The referee Miguel Ángel Ortiz, struggling to control this, went to the screen where he saw Romero’s studs hit Bellingham’s knee. The decision was reversed, the Englishman’s yellow taken away and shown to the Argentinian instead. The hosts still felt it should have been red for Bellingham. When Lee’s studs went in on Federico Valverde’s ankle, Real did too. Confrontations continued, words exchanged, but chances didn’t come. At half-time Atlético’s goalkeeper coach and Real’s assistant were sent off.The second half began with Koke introduced and Baena forcing a save. It was Atlético’s first shot on target and the start of a different game. Their second soon after gave them the lead and an advantage that was even bigger. A long ball from David Hancko dropped into the run of Simeone and as he dashed into the area Huijsen dragged him down. Ortiz pointed to the spot. He was also called to the screen again – not to overturn the penalty but to change the colour of the card. Huijsen walked, Grimaldo scored and the Metropolitano exploded.View image in fullscreenReal Madrid’s Dean Huijsen fouls Giuliano Simeone leading to a penalty and a red card for the defender.Photograph: Juan Carlos Lucas/Zuma Press Wire/ShutterstockYou suspected Mourinho would too. First, he removed Guler and Vinícius to introduce Yan Diomandé and Rüdiger. Vinícius had done little and a readjustment was required but there have been times when decisions like this – the Brazilian’s removal in last year’sclásicowas the beginning of the end for Xabi Alonso – have caused splits. It did not improve things either. Instead, Real were oddly passive and Atlético doubled the lead. It came from the right where Lee, outstanding, worked the ball to Simeone. His low cross, bent behind Madrid’s back four, was perfect. Six yards out, David turned it in.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionStill Atlético came. Courtois made an extraordinary save from Romero and Konaté cleared off the line from Julián Alvarez. Real could do nothing, seemingly concerned only with limiting the damage. Oblak barely saw them. Real did not touch the ball in his area until they scored. Kylian Mbappé barely touched the ball anywhere. Inside Atlético’s half, a pigeon pecked the grass, uninterrupted.When Diomandé did at last dash into that space with 15 minutes to go, Oblak saved, the opportunity to make a match of this wasted. Or so it seemed until, from a dead ball that was too late even for them, Rüdiger headed in to spark a rebellion that would prove brief and incomplete, unlike Simeone’s week.Explore more on these topicsLa LigaAtlético MadridReal MadridEuropean club footballmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: ‘Mixed emotions’ for Farke as Leeds stay unbeaten with Crystal Palace stalemate | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Leeds enter the international break in fifth place in the Premier League after a goalless draw with Crystal Palace
Author: Will Unwin
Headline: Leeds enter the international break in fifth place in the Premier League after a goalless draw with Crystal Palace
Content: Tyrick Mitchell puts the ball in the net but his effort was ruled out for offside.Photograph: Ed Sykes/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenTyrick Mitchell puts the ball in the net but his effort was ruled out for offside.Photograph: Ed Sykes/Action Images/ReutersPremier League‘Mixed emotions’ for Farke as Leeds stay unbeaten with Crystal Palace stalemateWill Unwinat Elland RoadSun 20 Sep 2026 11.08 EDTLast modified on Sun 20 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GooglePerhaps it is testament to the progress Leeds have made since returning to the Premier League just over a year ago that there was frustration at failing to move up to third after drawing withCrystal Palace. Instead, Daniel Farke’s team enter the prolonged international break in fifth and unbeaten, which is a fine achievement in itself.Apart from Tyrick Mitchell’s disallowed goal, neither side gave much impression they would secure the points. For Palace, it was a first clean sheet of the season, having conceded at least twice in their opening four games, relieving pressure on Pierre Sage, while the hosts endured their first blank.Semenyo helps chaotic Manchester City beat Sunderland 5-3 after Brobbey hat-trickRead moreA victory by two clear goals would have meant a best-ever start to a Premier League campaign for Leeds but they were blunt in the final third. There was even a level of discontent amid a ponderous performance with fans chanting “forward” as they failed to replicate thethrashing of Newcastleon Monday.“Mixed emotions,” Farke said. “We would have preferred to win, but the reality is it is 38 game days. It is not always magic nights under the floodlights, champagne football, you overrun the opponent and score goals for fun. Sometimes it is a scruffy Sunday afternoon when you have to dig in. This was one of these games.”Farke is into the final year of his contract and signing a new deal is a priority for him and the club. His stature has grown over the past 10 months, with Leeds the fifth-best performing team in the division since December 2025 and the German will likely be rewarded in the coming weeks for bringing stability to the club as Leeds aim to build on strong foundations.The most notable moment of the opening quarter here came when Walter Benítez took too long to distribute the ball. The referee, Adam Herczeg – making hisPremier Leaguedebut and fully aware of the rules – awarded Leeds a corner as punishment. It was a tentative game in the autumn sunshine, lacking intensity and quality, with Ao Tanaka snatching at a shot the closest anyone got to threatening a goal.Around the half-hour something akin to a football match broke out as nervousness was replaced by urgency. Jørgen Strand Larsen and Quinten Timber engineered a chance for Palace which was blocked and allowed Leeds to break through Noah Okafor down the left, although his cross was turned behind.Palace had the greater quality, with Adam Wharton and Timber comfortable in possession in the middle of the park, while Yéremy Pino whizzed around in the hope of finding an opener. It was controlled play, as the visitors took their time in the buildup, although there was often very little at the end of it as James Trafford was left unthreatened.View image in fullscreenJames Justin stretches to block an effort from Eddie Nketiah.Photograph: Greig Cowie/ShutterstockLeeds on the other hand would burst into life for brief moments as the full-backs flew forward, changing the dynamic in an instant but Palace’s centre-backs and wing-backs were built to deal with these rapid transitions, leaving Dominic Calvert-Lewin starved of service. Benítez could relax and re-read the laws of the game, having failed to face a single shot on target in the opening 40 minutes.Palace pushed the fast-forward button at the break and Mitchell put the ball in the back of the net from a fine move down the right. The glory turned to anguish when the video assistant referee intervened to show Anan Khalaili was offside in the buildup, causing an eruption inside Elland Road.Leeds were sluggish but the warning from Mitchell caused a reaction and they were almost ahead when Calvert-Lewin’s only real chance was saved by Benítez. The England striker was given too much space to get on the end of a cross but his sidefooted volley was weak.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionSemenyo helps chaotic Manchester City beat Sunderland 5-3 after Brobbey hat-trickRead moreThere was a touch of menace in the game as Tanaka and Wharton were booked in quick succession, the first for a cynical foul and the latter after lunging in late without a hope of winning the ball, ensuring Herczeg was far busier than the two goalkeepers.Leeds were completely ineffective in open play, Ethan Ampadu engaged in a long-throwathon. Every few minutes he would trot to a sidelineto pick up the ball and hurl it into the box but Palace were alive to the danger. “We had many set pieces today, but also today we didn’t have the best quality of the delivery,” Farke said.Palace edged the match and Daichi Kamada could have won it late on but his header drifted inches wide. Sage will be relieved to see his defence so well organised and untroubled after conceding 11 in the first four games, leading to plenty of early scrutiny on his appointment. “Especially when I read the social media, there’s a big pressure.” Sage said.“But you know, I don’t care about that. I do my job with honesty, I give my best with my skills and my limits. And in the end, I have no regrets with what I do.”Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueLeeds UnitedCrystal Palacematch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Rangers and Ryan Naderi finish off Celtic’s horror week with Old Firm victory | Scottish Premiership | The Guardian
description: With no away fans present at Celtic Park, Rangers beat Celtic for the second time in a week, winning 1-0 thanks to Ryan Naderi’s goal
Author: Jonathan Liew
Headline: With no away fans present at Celtic Park, Rangers beat Celtic for the second time in a week, winning 1-0 thanks to Ryan Naderi’s goal
Content: Ryan Naderi screams with joy after his goal, which ended up beating Celtic.Photograph: Kirk O’Rourke/Rangers FC/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenRyan Naderi screams with joy after his goal, which ended up beating Celtic.Photograph: Kirk O’Rourke/Rangers FC/ShutterstockScottish PremiershipRangers and Ryan Naderi finish off Celtic’s horror week with Old Firm victoryJonathan Liewat Celtic ParkSun 20 Sep 2026 10.11 EDTLast modified on Sun 20 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIf ever a stadium can be rocked by silence, this was the moment. With no visiting fans allowed at any of this season’s Glasgow derbies, Ryan Naderi’s winning goal was met with nothing but the banging of fists of the clear plastic of theRangersbench, and the shouting of the broadcast commentators. A screaming void of apathy and atrophy, the sound of a beckoning abyss, of a title race blowing open and a team slowly breaking apart.That Rangers were unable to celebrate this triumph with their fans in the stadium was, of course, a source of lament, as well as a measure of just how ugly this fixture has become over the years.It has become a day that is no longer relished but dreaded, a failure not just of the two fanbases themselves but the authorities who have allowed the ugliness to fester, who have talked a tough game on sectarianism but done little in practice to combat it at source.Celtic 0-1 Rangers: Scottish Premiership – as it happenedRead moreBut nothing could spoil the mood of Derek McInnes’s team, humming after a tough start to the season and now able to toast a second victory over theirrivals in the space of a week. For Celtic, sitting on three straight defeats, the silence will be filled with plenty of noises and voices over the coming international break: awkward questions and painful decisions that last season’s dramatic double may have forestalled but which can no longer be avoided.The drop in standards over the opening weeks of this season has been alarming, and at 74 years of age Martin O’Neill is wise enough and self-aware enough to know that he may be as much part of the problem as part of the solution. For him, the next few weeks will be a time of “self-reflection” on his role and his future, on whether he truly has the energy in him for one last fight.“It’s a matter of whether I can help the team, and I’ll have a look at that this week,” he said. “Every time things don’t go so well, age plays a part, and you know what, they may be right. I’m 110 in two years’ time. That may be time to wrap it up. But I’ll see how it goes.View image in fullscreenTempers flare between Rangers manager Derek McInnes (right) and his opposite number, Martin O’Neill, at Celtic Park.Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA“Let me generalise a little bit. I got an opportunity to come back last October which I never thought would happen in my life. Winning the league, the game against Hearts, was one of the great moments of my managerial time. But even then, I was still thinking about whether you can still have the energy, the desire. There’s nothing great about getting old, I’ll tell you that.”What is true of O’Neill may also be true of a few of his players. Is Callum McGregor, club legend but now 33 years of age and increasingly off the pace, still fit for purpose? Does Liam Scales need replacing? Does Kieran Tierney still have the legs? What exactly is James Forrest still doing about the place? And in the meantime, would you remotely trust theCelticboard – still essentially hollow of footballing expertise – to oversee the required transition?Not on this evidence. The summer signings – Kasper Høgh, Mika Baur, Camilo Durán – largely disappeared from view.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionQuick GuideRoundup: Vrancken bewildered by VAR as Hearts frustrated at KilmarnockShowWouter Vrancken was left bewildered by the “strange” video assistant referee decision to rule out an earlyHeartsgoal in their 1-1 draw at bottom-placedKilmarnock. The Jambos thought they had gone ahead in the 11th minute when Laurent Mendy’s effort – which appeared to be going wide – was diverted into the net by the Killie defender Cathal McCarthy. But the VAR, Matthew MacDermid, advised Duncan Nicolson to rule it out as the ball had accidentally struck Mendy’s hand. Killie went ahead a few minutes later through a Jamie McCart own goal before Stephen Kingsley equalised in the 86th minute (pictured).But Vrancken cited similarities with the recent incident involving Manchester United’s Harry Maguire against Ipswich and felt Mendy’s inadvertent handball should have been rendered irrelevant by McCarthy heading the ball into the net. “For me, when it’s such a clear situation, it’s strange that the VAR comes in between and rules wrong,” said the Belgian. “We had a meeting last week about the laws of the game and the refs did their explanation but when you don’t see them applied in the game, then I’m thinking this is strange."Martin Boyle endedHibernian’s losing streak at home after they fought back to claim a point in a 1-1 draw againstAberdeen. The Dons went ahead in the 17th minute with a composed finish from former Hibs striker Kevin Nisbet. Managerless Hibs – with John Potter in interim charge after David Gray’s midweek sacking – looked bereft of confidence for long spells. However, the Leith side – who had lost six successive games at Easter Road – earned a share of the spoils when Boyle levelled from the penalty spot in the 62nd minute after Jack Milne dragged Jason Kerr to the ground.Steven Pressley praised Joe Westley for the bravery he showed by playing inDundee's 2-1 home win overMotherwell. The former Burnley striker fractured his cheekbone against Hearts a fortnight ago but declared himself available after deciding against having surgery. Instead, he played wearing a protective mask and nett Dundee’s opening goal from the penalty spot before Bradley Fink doubled their advantage. Alex Lowry pulled one back for the visitors just before the break but the home side held on.Pressley said: “Joe showed great courage. But he gave a wonderful performance, without any trepidation. Joe was fearless in everything he did and to score a goal is really important for him because he lives off them."Jim Goodwin hailed his side’s performance as the perfect tonic asDundee Uniteddefeated StMirren3-0 in a one-sided contest in Paisley, with first-half goals from Jesse Randall, Lyall Cameron and Kevin Ciubotaru. It was Goodwin’s first appearance in the dugout since a recent health scare and the United manager said: “On a personal note, it was great to be back. Certainly the best medicine that I could have hoped for was that type of result and performance."A stunning set-piece strike from Enes Alic in the sixth minute of stoppage time secured a dramatic 1-1 draw for 10-manSt JohnstoneagainstFalkirk. Falkirk took advantage of Cheick Diabaté’s 54th-minute red card to seize the lead through Ethan Ross on the hour. But Alic found the top corner from 25 yards to move Simo Valakari’s side up to sixth place.Press AssociationPhotograph: Mark Runnacles/Shutterstock EditorialWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.There was fury here but precious little focus, plenty of passion but no real patterns of play, no order to the chaos, no real idea of how to keep the ball or fashion a chance.
